He then tells Bang to get down and launches a massive attack at the meteor. Genos attack proves too little to stop the meteor and he drains himself of energy and falls to the ground. At this point, Saitama shows up and asks Bang to take care of Genos and then promptly launches himself headlong towards the meteor. He quickly arrives at the meteor and punches himself through it, the meteor cracking up and exploding in his wake. The pieces of the meteor then start to rain on Z-City, destroying a bunch of buildings, including the one Genos and Bang are on. Saitama then lands, looks around, and nonchalantly walks away. Three days after the Meteor incident Saitama and Genos are relaxing in their apartment watching the news about the devastation the meteor fragments caused. Genos states that if the Hero Association had asked Saitama to help in the first place then the damage would have been reduced. After a brief discussion, Genos reveals that the incident raised their hero rankings: Saitama went from Class-C rank 342 to rank 5, Genos went from Class-S rank 17 to rank 16, and even Bofoi went up in rank from Class-S rank 7 to rank 6. Saitama is severely shocked by the jump in his position. After another brief discussion about Disaster Levels, Saitama decides to go for a walk. As Saitama is walking around Z-City, taking note of the destruction, he is accosted by Tanktop Tiger. Tiger accuses Saitama of taking credit for the meteor incident that he did not deserve. Saitama blows off these accusations, which angers Tiger, who then calls out his brother. Tanktop Black Hole then makes his entrance and the two brothers then accuse Saitama of cheating again. Saitama seems rather put off by this and asks the two what they plan on doing about it. Tiger starts to threaten Saitama with violence but is cut off by his brother who states that he knows the cruelest way to punish Saitama. Black Hole then takes a deep breath and in an extremely loud voice starts calling out Saitama, stating that he's to blame for the destruction of the town. As he goes on like this, citizens from the area start to gather on the group. Eventually, some of the citizens start to join in. At that point, Black Hole calls on Saitama to resign, which the citizens agree too. As this is happening, Bang is watching nearby from the roof of a building. He expresses his disappointment in the citizens and states that he'd rather see Saitama resign from the Hero Association than to see him corrupted by it. At this point, Black Hole goes to make his "decisive" move. He acts shocked and acts like Saitama made a move to start attacking the citizens. He and Tiger then step forward and state that they will "protect" the citizens by taking Saitama down. At this point Bang leaves, stating that he'd rather not watch a "public execution." Tanktop Tiger then steps forward and challenges Saitama first. He charges forward only to be casually knocked off into the distance by Saitama. Black Hole, enraged by this jumps forward and grabs Saitama's hands, only to fall to his knees due to the pain of having his hands being crushed by Saitama. He starts apologizing profusely, stating that he lied and that he gives up. Saitama interrupts him at this point, saying to everyone in the area that it was, in fact, his fault that the destruction was his fault and that if anyone had a problem with it that they should say it to his face. Someone tries to interrupt, but Saitama cuts him off stating that he is not a hero for the people's admiration, he does it because he feels like it. Several days later a Mysterious Being is seen walking up from the ocean.

Giant Salamander Giant Salamander (大山椒魚, "Ōsanshō̄o") was a Mysterious Being from the "One-Punch Man" OVAs. It was killed by Atomic Samurai. Appearance. Giant Salamander was a giant salamander monster with four red eyes and six legs. It had mostly dark green skin, with the lower half of his face along and entire stomach being mahogany. There were also many spots all over its body. Appearances in Other Media. OVAs. Going Fishing with Middle-aged Men. Giant Salamander is being pursued by Chain'n'toad and Mumen Rider, and it hides in a lake where Kamikaze and Bang are fishing. The two young heroes try to stop it, but fail, and Chain'n'toad is eaten by the Salamander. They are then saved by Atomic Samurai, who kills the monster and frees Chain'n'toad from its stomach. Abilities and Powers. Giant Salamander was capable of easily toying with both Mumen Rider and Chain Toad. This was largely due to its physical strength and mobility in the water, where it intentionally led the heroes to gain the upper hand. Although he somewhat acknowledged Chain Toad's strength when the latter was able to briefly restrain the monster with his Kusarigama, once he got serious he was able to quickly dispatch the A-Class hero.

Giant Snowman Giant Snowman (ダルマン, "Yuki Daruman") was a Mysterious Being that arose from a mountain. It was presumably killed by Saitama. Appearance. Giant Snowman was a colossal monster, towering well over a mountain. Its body consisted of a single giant snowball and a snowball head. It had dark arms, a small pointy nose, and thick eyebrows. History. This monster was created as snowmen around a snowy mountain became self aware and merged into one. Small and powerless in the beginning, it gradually absorbed the snowmen nearby and became an extremely dangerous giant. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapter. 200 Yen. The monster appears in the mountains, as Saitama is carrying a child on his shoulders. The fight between this monster and Saitama is not shown. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level threat, it can be assumed that Giant Snowman was a powerful Mysterious Being. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: Due to its enormous size, it can be presumed that Giant Snowman possessed great strength.

Giant Spaceship The Giant Spaceship was the headquarters and mode of transportation of the Dark Matter Thieves. It crashed after its power core was shattered as a result of the final clash between Saitama and Boros. The ship was later salvaged by Bofoi, who uses it to develop new technology. Appearance. In the manga and anime, the ship is shaped like a tooth. In the manga, the ship is colored Steel Black, while in the anime, it is Purple. The ship was massive in size; it was large enough to cast a shadow over the majority of A-City and was able to destroy 99.8% of the city with a single shell bombardment directed downward. The interior was equipped with numerous surveillance cameras, and each area was sealed with strong doors, which have repelled many intruders. Abilities and Powers. The Giant Spaceship was an extremely massive and powerful vehicle used by Boros and the Dark Matter Thieves to invade countless planets and travel across the entire universe.

Gigakigan Gigakigan (ギガキガン, "Gigakigan") was a Mysterious Being who was a rock with his own will. He was killed by Tatsumaki. Appearance. Gigakigan had a humanoid appearance, his entire body was made of rocks. Two horns could be seen protruding from either side of his head. Personality. Gigakigan considered himself the ultimate life form. He held a grudge against humans for wiping away his comrades "the minerals" through mining. As such, eradicating humanity became his goal. History. He had been enveloped in magma and collected energy for over a thousand years before awakening. During those thousand years, he witnessed his fellow brethren be mined away by humans. Appearances in Other Media. Omake. Tatsumaki's Day Off. He awakens in an unknown city and prepared to wreck havoc, but is quickly defeated by Tatsumaki. Abilities and Powers. Although Gigakigan's disaster level is unknown, he had been shown to possess enormous physical strength and durability. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: Gigakigan was large and possessed monstrous strength, able to effortlessly push a cliff-side apart. Immense Durability: Gigakigan withstood years of magma and smoldering.

Gish Gish (ギッシュ, "Gisshu") is the bureau director (局長) of the Z-City Hero Association Branch. Appearance. Gish is a well-dressed man with a portly figure. He has a slightly tank-shell shaped head, thick eyebrows, beady eyes, a fat freckle spotted nose, and gray hair. His facial features possess a particular sheen to them similar to polished wax. Like many associate officers, he wears a basic black suit with a white undershirt and sports a black tie. Personality. Initially appearing as a serious, stern individual, Gish true colors show to be that of a sleazy business man, one of a greedy sort to boot, willing to lie about the particular value of profitable ventures just to keep his investments safe. As well as withholding the particular danger notices of a case even at the cost of lives. In that he's shown to be a bit incompetent as well as arrogant, openly threatening his associates of assisted duplicity when his plans go south on top of leaving five lower class heroes to it and hoping for the best. Appearances in Other Media. Omakes. Squadron. When the Wolf Level Threat Scaledon had escaped the special confinement cell created by Dr. Bofoi, Director Gish, head of the Z-City Heroes Association branch network arranged to have a team of B ranked heroes assembled in order to apprehend the creature before word got out of his possibly illicit activities of profiteering off of the monsters scales. To that end he falsified a story about it without telling his retainer stating that the creatures blood and biology are of potent pharmaceutical value, and that such a finding must be kept a secret lest other rival organizations caught wind of such a discovery before they could retrieve it. While in his office with said worker who relayed the information he openly admitted such a statement to be a lie; having in truth, already set up a buyer who would purchase the beasts shedding's so he could make a good sum of money. When his assistant got a phone text from Metal Knight regarding the possible dangers of a monster increase in appearance and aggression's dependent upon a shift in its environment. The director immediately forbade his secretary from calling HQ for upper tier help threatening him of consequences that would ensue for both of them, the minuet his scheme was found out by the higher ups. Worriedly stating that despite it being weaker heroes they sent after, they were still five to one so they should let it play out. After the issue with Scaledon had been settled, The S-Class hero Bofoi had him laid off in light of his monumental screw up, at least until the heat died down in order to reinstate him as head of the Z-City department.

Glasses Glasses (メガネ, "Megane") is the B-Class Rank 21 professional hero of the Hero Association. He is one of the few people aware of Saitama's strength. Appearance. Glasses is an average-looking young man with black hair and a pair of black-frame glasses. Before his departure from the Blizzard Group, his outfit consisted of a standard black business suit and a white shirt. As an independent hero, he wears a green tracksuit with two white stripes running down his sleeves and pant legs. He also has multiple scars on his left arm. Personality. Originally wanting to become a hero, Glasses trained hard in order to become one. He, however, began losing self-confidence after becoming part of the Blizzard Group, believing that he and any other average person have limits and cannot keep up with people who have natural-born talent. After he was saved by Saitama and heard his opinion, Glasses realized that the only one that had put limits on him was himself, with his thinking of not being good enough to be a hero. After becoming much stronger, he reiterates this idea to Eyelashes. Since meeting Saitama, Glasses has begun training again, and has become far more level-headed and confident, remaining calm against Garou and even standing and fighting against him despite the danger that the martial artist posed. Even after being rendered unable to move and half-conscious, he possessed the will to report his location and summon Genos. History. Originally an office worker who had to cut down on food costs to survive, Glasses started his hero career to improve his lifestyle. He was able to climb to the B-Class. In order to retain his position, he joined the Blizzard Group. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Glasses is seen with Stinger, Wild Horn, Chain'n'toad, Smile Man, Gun Gun and Shooter as a part of the team led by Death Gatling to ambush the injured Garou. During the battle, he supports the group by resupplying Shooter's arrows but avoids attacking Garou directly. When Garou tries to target him anyway, Glasses throws rocks in his face as a distraction and follows up with a punch to the face. He then retreats to a far distance and leaves Garou open to the other heroes. However, Garou grows stronger and overpowers most of the other heroes. Garou targets Glasses a second time, closing the distance and chasing him down (so that Death Gatling cannot open fire), and simultaneously taunting Glasses for his strength. Glasses attempts to throw rocks at Garou again, but Garou catches them all and throws them at Shooter. Stinger briefly intercepts Garou but is quickly defeated. Glasses is incapacitated shortly thereafter, despite valiantly trying to throw a punch at Garou, when Garou knocks him out by elbow striking him toward a tree. Fortunately, he manages to send an emergency signal to Genos, who promptly arrives. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. A New Wind Blows. Glasses and twenty other members of the Blizzard Group corner and take down the C-Class criminal, Banero. However, Glasses did not actively participate in the fight because he was deep in thought and therefore gets no credit. When the Blizzard Group faces the Demonic Fan, Glasses witnesses how powerless he is. Suddenly, Tatsumaki enters the scene and, after berating Glasses for how useless he is, shatters the machine monster with one move before taking Fubuki away. Saitama soon arrives and is told by him that the fight is over. However, Demonic Fan's remnants reassemble itself and it comes back to life. As Saitama eagers to fight it, Glasses stops him, saying that a mere C-Class hero cannot possibly beat the monster. He goes on by claiming that normal humans have limits and that is what seperates them from ones with actual talent. In an instant, Saitama destroys the monster with a single punch, and motivates Glasses to keep moving forward, much to his shock. After Saitama leaves, Glasses realizes that the only one that had put limits on him was himself. He then leaves the Blizzard Group and continues his hero career with his own strength. Growth Process. Glasses stops a robbery at a grocery store, where he encounters his old comrade, Eyelashes. They chat and discuss each other's situation where Eyelashes praises Glasses on his improvement although Glasses denies that and he has much more to improve on. An explosion erupts in the distance and Glasses heads towards it. Eyelashes stops him as he doesn't believe he can stop the monster on his own. Glasses states his conviction to grow and leaves Eyelashes to call Fubuki. Eyelashes watches Glasses leave as he informs of a hero on the scene of the disaster. Abilities and Powers. Glasses is one of the higher-ranked B-Class heroes, and Garou noted that he is skilled in hand-to-hand combat. He was notably the only member of the Blizzard Group to avoid the Demonic Fan's second attack. Glasses was a part of Death Gatling's hero squad tasked with Garou's capture. Death Gatling notes the heroes as elites and praises their capabilities and experiences to survive life‐or‐death crises. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Durability: Glasses is shown to be quite resilient. He took a beating from a weakened Garou, withstanding long enough to attempt to for an attack again. Although it was noted by Stinger and Death Gatling that Garou was toying with him. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: During his fight against Garou, Glasses was shown to have developed decent speed, reflexes, and hand-to-hand combat skills from his independent training. He was able to dodge Garou's attempt to grab and use him as a shield, and always kept a certain distance from the Hero Hunter so as not to let him flee. Enhanced Strength: After weeks of physical training due to Saitama's advice, Glasses gained a considerable amount of physical strength to the point where he was able to somewhat hold his own against Garou, whose strength rivaled an S-Class hero, albeit the Hero Hunter was significantly weakened when fighting him. Enhanced Stamina and Endurance: Glasses declared to Garou that he has confidence in his stamina and persistence to continue the fight to the end. Despite all his damage, he stayed conscious long enough to call for help. It should be noted that he was also the only member of the squad to stay conscious after the fight. Tracking: Glasses is skilled at tracking targets as seen by how he was appointed to do so during the operation against Garou. Advanced Growth Rate: As a result of his consistent training, Glasses' strength grew over time as he was able to move up a rank in a short amount of time. Glasses' growth rate allows him to easily keep up with high-ranked heroes, as shown during the fight with Garou. Eyelashes noted his improvement after his training, when he managed to catch a kick to the head from him. Fighting Style. Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Glasses is proficient in fighting, knowing how to hold fighting stances and throwing punches although he prefers to wear out his opponent's stamina. He also has ranged attacks in which he throws several rocks at the opponent. Equipment. Emergency Transmitter: Glasses carries an emergency transmitter to request help from other nearby heroes in an emergency. Rocks: Glasses uses rocks to fight, utilizing them as projectile weapons against opponents.

Gluttonous Squirrels Gluttonous Squirrels (暴食リス, "Bōshoku Risu") was a group of squirrel-like monsters appeared in E-City Thrill Animal Park. They were apparently killed by Drive Knight. Appearance. The Gluttonous Squirrels were squirrels with four eyes, sharp teeth, and clawed fingers. Plot. Neo Hero Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. After monsterizing in the E-City Thrill Animal Park, they were presumably destroyed by Drive Knight and Genos, when the two arrived to fight the monsterized herbivores. Abilities and Powers. As a Wolf-level threat, it can be assumed that the Gluttonous Squirrels was relatively weak. They were likely easily eliminated by Drive Knight, a high-ranked S-Class hero.

Go! Saitama Go! Saitama is a One-Punch Man Animated Short Film that was conceived and directed by series' Manga Illustrator, Yusuke Murata. The Short is 107-seconds long and was animated by Murata himself along with his team at Village Studio. Go! Saitama was posted to Yusuke Murata's twitter account September 23, 2021. In his post, Murata expressed his desire to further develop his skills and to add voices, music and sound effects to future animation efforts. He added that he would like to make not only One-Punch Man animations, but also animations for various other works. Summary. Go! Saitama begins with the titular hero effortlessly defeating a monster, only for the blowing wind to carry a Grocery Store Catalogue towards his bald head. Upon reading it, Saitama discovers the existence of a 1-yen (about US$0.01) sale for high-grade hot-pot meat — but there's a catch, said sale will come to an end at exactly 5:00 p.m. that day. Never one to waste an opportunity when it comes to a bargain deal, the caped hero sets out for his destination. Saitama sprints with tremendous speed, leaving a great trail of dust in his wake, but nearly collides a building as he checks his wristwatch to confirm what time it is — learning that he only has a few minutes left until the sale ends. Desperate, the hero rushes through a river and leaps over the city to make his way in time, but is forced to slow down in order to help an old lady cross the street. When it looks like the complications are over, Saitama is met with his greatest obstacle yet: Two trains closing in as cross the rails in opposite directions. Believing that he is fast enough to rush past the speeding trains, Saitama puts his mind on the task and accelerates in a dashing blur, but is unfortunately unable to make it in time, crashing against the second train. Thankfully, the hero is able to narrowly avoid colliding with any of the terrified passengers inside and makes his way out the other end on the train, immediately resuming his journey for the hot-pot sale. However, all of Saitama's efforts would seemingly be in vain, as when he finally arrives on the Grocery Store he is confronted with a long, winding line reaching across the block. Curious and confused, the hero steps inside the store to see what the commotion is about, only to discover that the line is for an autograph booth with S-Class Hero Puri-Puri Prisoner — and, more importantly, that the 1-yen hot-pot meat bargain sale has just expired. Distraught and defeated, Saitama collapses onto the floor in frustration, but is met his trusted apprentice Genos, who reveals that he had already come to the Grocery Store and bought the hot-pot ahead of him. Smiling, Saitama and Genos set out for their home, grocery bag in tow.
Gobrich Gobrich (ゴブリッチ, "Goburitchi") is the Hero Association's Junior Hero Strengthening Office Section Chief.

God An enigmatic entity referred to as God (カミ, "Kami") by several individuals such as Homeless Emperor, Psykos, and Blast. It serves as overarching antagonist of the Monster Association Arc, controlling and empowering several major villains. Appearance. In its first appearance, "God" looked like a swirling gust of wind with scribbles that outline a person. "God" is described by Psykos as reminiscent of Jupiter's surface with countless spiraling spots overlapping over one another. When Saitama, Flashy Flash, and Manako peered through a hole while they were underground, "God" seemingly appeared to be in another dimension and it looked like an extremely massive humanoid entity, so much so that it completely dwarfed the hole they peered into. However, none of the three could see it. When making its second appearance in Homeless Emperor's vision, it looked like a giant humanoid figure made entirely out of flesh and bones with no face. It is unknown whether its physical form is the same, if it even has one, or if they were just imaginary projections in Homeless Emperor's mind. When making an appearance in a vision to Tatsumaki and Garou, "God" impersonated Blast's appearance as he was when Blast first met Tatsumaki and Bang for Garou. The facade quickly faded to display its true faceless appearance once the trick failed to work for either of them. Personality. "God" gave Homeless Emperor its powers and enhanced the abilities of Orochi and Psykos, although its motives remain unknown. "God" appears to agree with Homeless Emperor's belief that humanity is a worthless plague on an otherwise grand and beautiful planet. It also has a tendency to test whether people are worthy of receiving its power through a mysterious cube. If found unworthy, they will face "forfeiture," presumably leading to their demise. "God" seems intent on keeping its existence hidden from most people if possible. This is demonstrated when it mercilessly takes back the powers it had granted to Homeless Emperor before the latter could answer any questions from Zombieman. Furthermore, "God" appears to be an opportunistic being, often manifesting before individuals who are in the depths of despair, disguising itself as someone they hold dear in order to tempt them with offers of power. After Garou's defeat at the hands of Saitama in the Ominous Future, "God" killed him while also taking back the powers it had given Garou in an attempt to prevent the Hero Hunter from passing onto Saitama a time travel technique that could undo Garou's bad actions. This indicates that this enigmatic entity will eliminate those whose actions go against its desires. While "God" seems to hate humans, it does not appear to value life on Earth in general. This is shown by Blast's warning that Garou in his Cosmic Fear Mode was still being manipulated by "God," with each of the Hero Hunter's attacks emitting deadly energy that threatened all living things on the planet. History. It's mentioned that in the past twenty years, Blast and his collaborators have been fighting "God". They were searching for and attempting to analyze the mysterious cubes, which allow communication with "God" and transform humans into Mysterious Beings. Two years ago, when Blast fought Elder Centipede, "God" interrupted the S-Class hero and offered him its powers. After refusing to accept its powers, Blast engaged in a fight with the mysterious entity and managed to survive. The sudden appearance of "God" was possibly the reason Elder Centipede could escape from the top-ranking hero. Since then, Blast decided to keep the existence of "God" from other people in the Hero Association. More than one month prior to Homeless Emperor meeting Zombieman, "God" granted the former his light powers. At some point in the past, "God" turned Empty Void into a Mysterious Being and made him its pawn while he and Blast were searching for the mysterious cubes. Consequently, Blast found himself in the painful position of having to confront and defeat Void, who had once been his partner. It was fifteen years ago that Blast emerged victorious in the battle, leaving Void with grave injuries that would take the aforementioned time to recover from. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. "God" is first seen in a flashback as Homeless Emperor recounts his backstory to Zombieman. He describes how he stumbled upon it in the park one day. It compliments Homeless Emperor for his "correct" ideology but states the human has no reason to die. Instead, it gave him the ability to summon and control energy spheres at will, telling the newly-empowered human he should know what to do with this power and leaving. During the fight between Orochi and Saitama deep underground, Orochi reveals a tablet he discovered in an ancient shrine, which depicted Orochi and stated that a worthy sacrifice was needed in order to resurrect "God", leading Orochi to believe this was referring to him. Soon after, the hero easily defeats Orochi with a single punch. Before the ancient cave collapses, his remnants crawl to the tablet while the full picture of the actual "God" appears in the mural and is not visible to the Monster King. "God" is later seen in another flashback as Psykos recounts how she obtained the source of her enhanced power. She describes it as a huge mass of brain cells with a similar appearance to that of Jupiter's surface. "God" later communicates to Saitama, Flashy Flash, and Manako after they touch a cube. The mysterious figure is surprised that there are three of them, before telling them to put their hands on the cube in order to either gain powers if they are worthy or face "forfeiture" if they are not. The three of them make no decision as Blast suddenly appears and confiscates the cube himself. Before the hero teleports the cube to an unknown location, "God" makes a final shocked comment as to the presence of Blast. After Homeless Emperor's defeat, when Zombieman begins inquiring more about the entity Homeless Emperor was speaking of, he suddenly sees a colossal figure appear and stand on top of the Moon. The entity then appears in his mind, only with its appearance being changed into a colossal giant of flesh and fractured bones. It then mercilessly takes away Homeless Emperor's light powers and his life, causing his body to disintegrate in the process. Later on, when Tatsumaki was down and near unconscious, "God" attempts to lure her into taking its powers, using Blast's own form to do so. However, it fails as Tatsumaki realizes that it is not the real Blast and simply asks "God" regarding its true identity. "God" then simply leaves in irritation. During the fight between Saitama and Garou, the latter's attack manages to weaken the dimensional seal keeping "God" at bay. In the sky, several large clouds formed, and through the clouds, God's feet appeared and began walking. As Garou was defeated by Saitama, "God" communicates with him through telepathy and offers him the power to defeat the Caped Baldy. While it impersonates Bang's appearance and offers Garou its hand, despite Garou realizing that somebody's impersonated his former master and just slapping its hand away, the mere act of him "touching" the hand of "God" was enough for him to be influenced by the mysterious entity. Before leaving and vanishing from Garou's sight, "God" states that it will make him its "avatar", with the Hero Hunter afterward nearly losing consciousness from the intense flow of power through his entire body. Despite being empowered by "God", Garou is still unable to prevail against Saitama. Upon discovering Tareo's death due to his fault, Garou repents and asks Saitama to copy his time travel technique in order to go back to the past and change the Ominous Future. Shortly after Garou begins to use his technique in front of Saitama, "God" kills the Hero Hunter by turning him into a statue of salt, taking back his powers in the process, although not before the Caped Baldy manages to master Garou's technique which he then uses to travel through time. Saitama returns to the past, arriving at the moment when Garou, shortly after achieving his Cosmic Fear Mode, appeared in front of many heroes. He lets out a powerful punch toward the Hero Hunter's face, defeating him before the Ominous Future could occur again. Soon, Saitama is thrown back into his "past" self and becomes one with him, having forgotten what's happened. Suffered defeat from a mysterious knockout punch, a confused Garou screams in pain as God's powers begin to leave his body, freeing him from the influence of the enigmatic entity. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. Following the Monster Association's downfall, an emergency meeting is held by Sitch, with Sekingar, Sweet Mask and only several S-Class heroes attending. The main topic of discussion is "God" who has the powers to telepathically communicate with and transform humans into Mysterious Beings. The heroes present are instructed to maintain secrecy about this threat until they can develop effective countermeasures. Sitch then reveals a message from Blast that "God" intervenes more frequently in the three-dimensional space where Earth resides because something (Saitama) in this dimension has caught its attention. Later, when Fubuki is on her way to meet Psykos at the Hero Association Headquarters, she recalls her encounter with the latter during the Monster Association raid. After defeating Psykos, Fubuki briefly sensed the presence of "God" while trying to figure out the source of Psykos' madness. Abilities and Powers. "God" possesses a wide range of supernatural powers and abilities, although the full extent of its powers remains largely unknown. The top-ranking S-Class hero, Blast, has been actively searching for cube-shaped objects associated with "God" in an attempt to prevent individuals from being bestowed powers by this enigmatic figure. Considering that Blast only takes action when humanity faces a true crisis, it can be inferred that "God" poses an exceedingly dangerous threat. After receiving what seem-to-be a fraction of power from "God", Garou underwent a transformative mutation and gained formidable abilities. He became capable enough to fight against and even force Saitama to get before ultimately being defeated. This event strongly suggests that "God" is phenomenally powerful due to being Garou's source of power. Additionally, Sitch mentions that opposing "God" requires the ability to manipulate space-time, which speaks volumes about the terrifying power of this mysterious entity. Considering the substantial evidence and consistent indications, it is likely that "God" exists as a higher-dimensional entity, with Blast unambiguously describing the dimension where it resides as a higher dimension. Supernatural Abilities. Power Bestowal: "God" can turn humans into Mysterious Beings, granting them supernatural powers. For instance, it bestowed upon Homeless Emperor the incredible ability to summon energy spheres resembling mini suns that explode upon contact, creating massive bursts of flames. Psykos and Orochi also received a massive power boost during their fusion, allowing them to slice through the Earth's surface with a single attack. Moreover, "God" can grant powers to individuals who place their hands on one of the mysterious cubes. However, those deemed unworthy face "forfeiture" and presumably death. It can also reclaim the granted powers along with the lives of the recipients. Thanks to the powers received from "God", Garou gained awareness of the flow of all energy and the behaviour of all forces in the cosmos; the Hero Hunter also having become capable of fighting against even a serious Saitama, albeit losing in the end. In addition, it granted Empty Void a powerful technique known as Dimensional Slash. Described by Blast as interference from a higher dimension, this technique possesses the remarkable ability to surpass conventional limitations such as distance, energy, and size. Mind Incursion: "God" has demonstrated the ability to infiltrate the minds of its targets, such as Homeless Emperor, and freely change the appearance of its projection within their minds. Besides, this ability allows it to find and disguise as someone its targets hold dear. It used this ability on Tatsumaki, taking on the appearance of Blast in an attempt to lure her into accepting its power, but failed. On the contrary, its attempt at Garou by imposing as Bang was a success, though the Hero Hunter accidentally received its power by slapping its hand away. Despite retaining part of his personality after being transformed by "God," Garou remained susceptible to its mental influence, which made him much more cruel than before. Telepathy: "God" can mentally communicate with humans on Earth. It once used telepathy to communicate with Flashy Flash, Saitama, and Manako after they had touched a mysterious cube, which allows for contacting it. However, it is also capable of establishing contact without the need for physical contact with the cube, as evident when it approached Garou after his defeat by Saitama. Additionally, following the Monster Association incident, Sitch held an emergency meeting with Sekingar and a few S-Class heroes to discuss how to deal with the possibility of anyone becoming a monster through telepathic communication with "God". Supernatural Awareness: "God" seems to possess an increased sense of awareness across dimensions. The Moon, in particular, is highly likely to be associated with this enigmatic figure. There are multiple instances where the Moon appears during significant battles between the Hero Association and the Monster Association, as if it is an eye watching the battlefield. Additionally, "God" is seemingly able to sense and manifest before individuals who are in the depths of despair, tempting them with offers of power, as seen with Homeless Emperor. Blast has also stated that this entity intervenes more frequently in the three-dimensional space where Earth resides because something (Saitama) has caught its attention. Time Manipulation: When Saitama, Flashy Flash, and Manako were underground in Z-City near a mysterious cube, Blast stated that their surroundings experienced a slower flow of time compared to other places and advised them to leave quickly. The cube, presumably created by "God", caused this time dilation. It's possible that the cube serves as a manifestation of power from "God" and shares its traits, suggesting this entity's capacity to affect time to some degree. Another piece of evidence is that Garou's time travel technique, which he passed onto Saitama, was recognized by the Hero Hunter as a power derived from "God." Spatial Manipulation: "God" possesses the capability to manipulate space, enabling it to open portals or dimensional rifts from which its feet can emerge. The mysterious cubes, which are presumed to be created by "God" and potentially serve as a manifestation of its power, also induce spatial distortion in their vicinity, as stated by Blast. Furthermore, this entity bestowed upon Empty Void one of its formidable powers known as Dimensional Slash, a technique that surpasses the normal constraints of distance and likely allows its wielders to cleave through the fabric of space itself. Dimensional Travel: "God" is able to traverse between dimensions. According to Blast, "God" was on the verge of breaking through a dimensional barrier. Its feet were seen emerging from mysterious thunderclouds, which appeared to be dimensional rifts. Blast also stated that "God" intervenes more frequently in the three-dimensional space where Earth is situated because something (Saitama) in this dimension has caught its attention. Invisibility: "God" can project images of itself and conceal its presence from those it wishes to remain unseen by. Many heroes, including Saitama, were unable to see its feet emerging from dimensional rifts. Miscellaneous Abilities. Cosmic Knowledge: Due to having imparted Garou the immense knowledge of the universe, it can be presumed that "God" is also extremely knowledgeable about the cosmos.

Goddess Glasses "Monster Princess" Goddess Glasses (怪人姫メガネメガミ, "Kaijin Ki Megane Megami") was a Demon-level Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association who claimed to have 999 love slaves. She was killed by Sweet Mask. Appearance. Goddess Glasses was a monster that resembled a human female. She wore heart-shaped glasses and a black dress. Personality. Goddess Glasses was a very ambitious individual who desired to become the planet's queen through use of her mind control. It can be inferred that she preferred being in control and that she had great confidence in her abilities as she has already taken control of 999 people before facing Sweet Mask. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Goddess Glasses fights Sweet Mask and attempts to make him her 1000th love slave but fails and is swiftly defeated by him. Abilities & Powers. As a high-ranked member of the Monster Association, Goddess Glasses was a powerful being. Supernatural Abilities. Mind Manipulation: Goddess Glasses possessed the ability to project a beam capable of turning her targets into "love slaves" regardless of their strength, who served her immediately afterward. Fighting Styles. Hypnosis: Goddess Glasses used her special energy beams in combat in order to hypnotize her opponents.

Gokiburi Buster Gokiburi Buster is a One-Shot manga written by ONE and illustrated by Summary. Humans may be considered at the top of the food chain, but when people are in the presence of cockroaches, they cower in fear. Who can they turn to when faced with these insects? The Gokiburi Busters, who have yet to fail to eliminate a threat!

Golden Ball Golden Ball (ボール, "Ōgon Bōru") is the A-Class Rank 26 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. Golden Ball is a tall man with blonde hair and a brown goatee. He wears baggy pants, a hoodie underneath a Letterman's jacket, and a white beanie. His jacket has "Golden Ball" printed on its back and on the left breast, and the right breast of his jacket has the words "It's not Kintama, its Golden Ball," a reference to a euphemism of testicles. Personality. Golden Ball is a rather confident man who believes he does not need to prepare for a fight. However, he has some experience with hunting and pretends to be drunk while Garou calls him out to the alleyway for a fight, only dropping his cover once he had attacked Garou by surprise. Plot. Hero Association Saga. Rumored Monster Arc. Golden Ball, along with Spring Mustachio, is dispatched to Z-City to investigate the rumors of an intensely strong monster. After not finding anything for a while, the two heroes catch a glimpse of a Mysterious Being and give chase. The creature turns out to be Kombu Infinity. Golden Ball immediately pulls out his weapon and fires a volley of his "Shape Memory Gold Balls" at Kombu Infinity who casually swipes away the attack to the side. While that was happening, Kombu Infinity was sneaking one of his tentacles through the street drain, and from behind, wrapped it around Golden Ball's leg. He pulls him down the road and throws him into the side of a building, rendering him unconscious and unable to fight. Golden Ball was later picked up by the reinforcements and taken to the hospital. Some time after the event, he received a promotion to rank 26. Human Monster Saga. Hero Hunt Arc. Golden Ball is drinking in a bar when Garou approaches him and challenges him to a fight. Golden Ball accepts, feigning drunkenness, and the two head to a parking lot to fight. His act dupes Garou into lowering his guard, and, in the alleyway on the way to the lot, he fires a shot that Garou barely manages to dodge. He launches a second shot, but Garou dodges it as well. Golden Ball realizes that Garou is predicting the path of the projectiles by reading his hand movements and fires a shot that ricochets and pierces Garou's leg. Golden Ball, believing he has the advantage now, follows up with Golden Breakout. However, Garou effortlessly dodges all of them, thus refuting Golden Ball's initial thought that Garou used Golden Ball's hand movements to dodge his bullets. In a final effort, Golden Ball fires one more shot directly at Garou. Unfortunately, Garou was able to deflect and destroy it and then destroys all of the other bullets. Before Garou can attack Golden Ball, Spring Mustachio appears, and while he is able to put Garou on the defensive for a period of time, is quickly defeated. Golden Ball warns Garou of his cockiness, only to hear Garou willfully disregard it until his defeat at the hands of a hero. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Pork Cutlet Bowl. Golden Ball was among the many heroes summoned by McCoy to combat the monster that was devastating the Z-City police station. He arrives at the scene late, after Saitama has already killed the monster. Abilities and Powers. As an A-Class hero, Golden Ball is a skilled and powerful fighter. The Hero Association considered him powerful enough to send to investigate mysteries of Z city along with Spring Mustachio. He was the first A-Class hero to harm Garou, something 5 of the top 10 in A-Class couldn't do, forcing Garou to use the Water Stream Rock Smashing Fist, something Garou only used on an S-Class hero before. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: Golden Ball demonstrates the strength needed to operate a slingshot that can pierce steel. Enhanced Speed: As an A-class hero, Golden Ball is quite fast. He was able to dash past a block with a few leaps. Enhanced Senses: Golden Ball's senses are sharp enough to accurately pinpoint the angles necessary to ricochet his golden balls and was able to hit Garou's leg, despite being intoxicated, and would've likely hit Garou's vitals had he not been drinking. Fighting Style. Expert Marksman: Golden Ball has an incredible aptitude in sharpshooting. Golden Ball can launch bullets that bounce off nearby surfaces towards a target to prevent the opponent from figuring out where the bullet is heading. His propensity for long-range combat also pairs well with his partner Spring Mustachio's skill in short-range combat. Equipment. Slingshot: Golden Ball carries a black, metallic slingshot. The slingshot bands can stretch the length of his arm. Attached to the base of the weapon is a laser pointer, which helps guide his shots. Golden Ball uses the slingshot to fire Shape Memory Gold Bullets at high speeds. Shape Memory Gold Bullets (形状記憶弾金, "Keijō Kioku Tamakin"): Golden Ball carries golden balls that change shape when fired. Hero Rating. Golden Ball's rating determined by the Hero Association:

Golden Sperm Golden Sperm (, "Ōgon Seishi"; Viz: Golden Spermatozoon) is a powerful fusion of Black Sperm's cells. He later merges with over 11 trillion of Black Sperm cells and becomes the ultimate fusion Platinum Sperm. In the original webcomic, Golden Sperm was defeated and killed by Garou. Appearance. Golden Sperm is a large and muscular humanoid that retains his previous self's head shape. His signature element is his overpowering golden shimmer which feeds directly into his many physical powers. Personality. Golden Sperm retains the arrogance that Black Sperm possesses, and has no issue looking down upon beings it views as inferior. He takes pleasure in using intimidation tactics and cruelty, but remains strategic in his thinking, agreeing with Homeless Emperor when the villain suggested leaving Fuhrer Ugly alive to further their own pursuits. Golden Sperm, exhibiting both cunning and ruthlessness, once intervened to rescue Homeless Emperor from Atomic Samurai's assault, despite his intentions of taking down Homeless Emperor later as Black Sperm. Following the severing of his forearm by Atomic Samurai, he demonstrates intense fury, vowing to exact a heavy toll from the hero. His sadistic nature becomes apparent as he menacingly advances toward Atomic Samurai, telling the other heroes to line up while declaring his intent to systematically eliminate them one by one. Additionally, despite his arrogance, Golden Sperm demonstrates a somewhat methodical approach to his actions. He cautions Black Sperm against attacking King recklessly and actively cooperates with Homeless Emperor in their united effort to confront the renowned hero. In the original webcomic, after his birth, Golden Sperm was quickly shown to have little interest in the livelihoods of the other Black Sperm cells, and even suggested absorbing them as they had become obsolete. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Upon being angered by Fuhrer Ugly's behavior and realizing that the heroes are largely distracted and weakened, Black Sperm merges a large number of his cells into Golden Sperm, who then attacks the fat monster for "crossing the line." Fuhrer Ugly attempts to fight back against Golden Sperm, but his acidic vomit is unable to harm the latter, who cites the anti-corrosive properties of gold as the reason why he is completely unfazed. Golden Sperm later witnesses Homeless Emperor appear and punish Fuhrer Ugly, who then leaves them out of their mercy. Soon, Golden Sperm switches his focus on Superalloy Darkshine, who is trembling in fear due to suffering damage from Fuhrer Ugly's digestive fluids before. Golden Sperm comments about Darkshine's unworthiness for being an S-Class hero shortly before landing a punch on his face, which sends the hero flying a considerable distance towards Iaian, Atomic Samurai and Spring Mustachio's whereabouts. These three heroes are then attacked by Homeless Emperor, who sends his energy orbs raining down on them. As Golden Sperm watches Iaian and Spring Mustachio being overwhelmed by Homeless Emperor's Extreme Carpet Bombing, Atomic Samurai finally manages to unsheathe the Sun Blade, which proceeds to possess him while simultaneously granting a massive power boost. The empowered S-Class hero saves Iaian and Spring Mustachio by dispersing a massive ball of energy that Homeless Emperor was about to attack them with. Atomic Samurai in his possessed state attempts to kill Homeless Emperor but in that moment, Golden Sperm saves him by blocking the Sun Blade with his right forearm. Golden Sperm initially wonders if the source of Atomic Samurai's power boost is monsterization, but quickly realizes that the Sun Blade is actually the source. Golden Sperm attempts to destroy the blade, but to his surprise, his right forearm ends up being sliced off instead. Before further damage can be done, the effects of the Sun Blade wear off and Atomic Samurai regains his senses. The S-Class hero is exhausted from wielding the Sun Blade, and Evil Natural Water shows up. The now enraged Golden Sperm states that Atomic Samurai will pay a high price for cutting off his arm and also tells the remaining heroes to form a line and wait for their turn to be killed. At this moment, King appears with his King Engine rumbling, causing Golden Sperm to stop in his tracks. Together with Black Sperm, Homeless Emperor and Evil Natural Water, Golden Sperm confronts the famous hero. Having grown paranoid and fearful of King's words and next movements, believing that the hero is looking down on him, Black Sperm is enraged and decides to merge all of his clones together in order to defeat him. Golden Sperm then combines with over 11 trillion of Black Sperm cells and becomes the ultimate fusion Platinum Sperm. Abilities and Powers. As a fusion of a mass number of cells of Black Sperm, a Mysterious Being that was already classified as a Dragon-level threat, Golden Sperm is extremely powerful. He possesses an extreme amount of raw power and speed, as demonstrated when he was capable of effortlessly defeating powerful individuals such as Fuhrer Ugly and Superalloy Darkshine, the former being a powerful Dragon-level monster while the latter being an S-Class hero well-known for his extraordinary strength and toughness. In the original webcomic, Sweet Mask stated that even if all of the S-Class heroes present fought Golden Sperm, it would still be a very difficult task to defeat him. He easily defeated a weakened Tatsumaki and moved so fast that the present heroes could not even see him in motion. Along with this, he was also able to fight against evolved Garou on equal footing, even if it was only for a few moments. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: Golden Sperm possesses tremendous physical strength; far surpassing the capabilities of his individual cells. He was able to thrash Fuhrer Ugly, a powerful Dragon-level threat, with little to no effort. Furthermore, Golden Sperm's strength is so overwhelming that he could knock out Superalloy Darkshine, a very formidable S-Class hero, and send him flying a fair distance away, with only a single punch. Immense Durability: Along with his immense strength, Golden Sperm also possesses amazing toughness. He was capable of taking sword slashes from Atomic Samurai, whose strength was further enhanced by the legendary Sun Blade, while only having his right forearm slightly penetrated against the hero's blade. However, Atomic Samurai was able to cut off the forearm when he exerted more power. Immense Speed and Reflexes: Golden Sperm is amazingly fast, as demonstrated when he was easily able to punch Fuhrer Ugly faster than the latter could react. Furthermore, he was fast enough to instantly appear in front of Homeless Emperor and defend the latter from Atomic Samurai. Immense Endurance: Even after getting his forearm cut off by Atomic Samurai, Golden Sperm showed no signs of pain and was prepared to continue fighting regardless of the heavy bleeding. Acid Resistance: Due to having the anti-corrosive properties of gold, Golden Sperm is extremely resistant to acid. When hit with a direct blast of acidic vomit from Fuhrer Ugly, he remained entirely unharmed—a stark contrast to Darkshine, whose skin was previously melted by the same substance. Fusion: Golden Sperm could fuse with all other Black Sperm cells to become the ultimate fusion Platinum Sperm. Psychic Resistance: In the original webcomic, Golden Sperm was able to effectively resist an injured Tatsumaki's psychic attacks. However, it has been confirmed that if she was in perfect condition, he would lose. Fighting Style. Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Golden Sperm primarily relies on his brute strength, preferring to throw simple but powerful punches.

Gomago Gomago (ゴマゴ, "Gomago") is a member of Narinki's Private Squad. Appearance. Gomago is a stocky man with strong muscles. He has a rather serious face and wears a white bandanna on his forehead, with black hair as well. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Gomago and the rest of his team are summoned by Narinki to save his son Waganma. Narinki states that if his squad retrieves his son, they will be paid very handsomely, so much so that even their grandchildren won't have to work. Gomago and the squad invade the Monster Association but are eventually overpowered and attempt to escape. Before they can escape, however, G5 intercepts them and brings them to Orochi and Gyoro Gyoro. Gomago and the rest of the team are absolutely terrified, and Gomago is staring nervously with sweat streaking down his face as the monsters contemplate what to do with them. Then, several monsters jump to kill them, but Royal Ripper murders them before they can reach the squad because he wants the pleasure all to himself. But then, G5 intervenes and says their battle suits are connected to their bodies. Royal Ripper still isn't convinced, but before he can torture them, Do-S stops his sword with her whip. She suggests to turn them into her love slaves, which Gyoro Gyoro agrees with. Gomago, along with the other mercenaries, are then turned into love slaves. When the heroes invade the headquarters, Do-S tells Gomago and the others to prepare for battle and kill any heroes that they come across. Eventually, Sweet Mask interrupts the battle and, after dismissing the disciples, intends on massacring the entire squad. However, the disciples quickly return and incapacitate Gomago and the other members of the squad, leaving Sweet Mask to deal with Do-S. When Do-S is taken down, the mind-controlling effect of her whip breaks, returning Gomago's humanity. He then joins several of the other squad members in gushing over Sweet Mask. Abilities and Powers. As a member of Narinki's Private Squad equipped with new battle armor from The Organization, Gomago has impressive abilities. Together with the squad, he was able to pressure Atomic Samurai's disciples, who are S-Class material according to Fubuki. Mercenary skills. When not using weapons, Gomago is very proficient in close-quarter combat and seems to use a fighting style based on wrestling moves. Just like his leader Tongara, Gomago can fake his emotions and trick others through acting, even though vicious monsters such as Royal Ripper are not easily affected by it. He was also able to replicate the behavior of a typical love slave of Do-S despite having experienced such a status only once. Equipment. Battle Suit: Gomago wears armor manufactured by The Organization provided to him by Narinki. The armor is even more advanced than the previous battle suits and allows him to fight top-ranking A-class heroes. Sword: Gomago wielded a sword that resembles a dadao, and was presumably proficient in wielding it. The sword was destroyed during the battle with Atomic Samurai's disciples.

Gotz Okkie The Gotz Okkie (ゴッツオッキー, "Gottsu Okkī") is an aircraft carrier. It was designed by Bofoi. Description. It is a large aircraft carrier with the hull number 52. It carried a large complement of jet fighters, electronic warfare aircraft, and helicopters, all of which fell into the sea after the carrier was nearly capsized by Evil Natural Water. The ship itself was not noticeably damaged by Evil Natural Water, but Saitama made a crater on the main flight deck in order to steer it and later jump towards Garou's whereabouts. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. While operating at sea in Z-City, Gotz Okkie is caught in the body of the newly-enlarged Evil Natural Water. The crew is evacuated below deck and the ship is freed from the anomaly after Saitama uses a Serious Punch to disperse the water monster, but is unable to regain control of Gotz Okkie's movement due to damages it has sustained earlier. Unable to pick up and carry the ship himself due to not having somewhere to stand on, Saitama elects to use the vessel's deck as an impromptu surfboard. To ensure the other heroes do not get hurt, Saitama positions and stops the ship while the crew seals up the bulkheads to prevent anymore water from entering the vessel.

Roaring Aura Sky Ripping Fist Whirlwind Water Stream: Roaring Aura Sky Ripping Fist (, "Senpū Ryūsui: Gōki Kūretsu-ken"; Viz: Whirling Wind Flowing Water: Fist of Roaring Qi, Rending Air), or simply Roaring Aura Sky Ripping Fist (, "Gōki Kūretsu-ken"; Viz: Fist of Roaring Qi, Rending Air), is a powerful martial art fighting style that combines Water Stream Rock Smashing Fist and Whirlwind Iron Cutting Fist together. Overview. This technique normally requires two combatants to be performed. To use the technique in pairs, Bang and Bomb stand side-by-side and assume strong stances. Both proceed to perform their respective martial arts, striking their opponent simultaneously. This results in the release of powerful shockwaves that surge through their target's body, causing devastating internal damage. The shockwave generated by this technique is so potent that it can pulverize surrounding debris into fine powder. In a remarkable display of its effectiveness, Bang and Bomb together were able to knock back a charging Elder Centipede and shatter the giant monster's hard exoskeleton. This impressive combined attack left Genos awestruck who labeled it the "ultimate technique." However, it is stated by Bang that they can only execute this technique once per battle since both of them have passed their prime. During the fight between a monsterized Garou and Bang, the former has demonstrated enough skills to not only be able to perform this technique alone by utilizing Bang's and Bomb's martial arts in each hand respectively, but Garou's capacities for it are also highly potent, which Bomb even remarks that should Bang endure a blow from Garou, the resulting shockwaves would fracture his bones. As Bang and Bomb together are only barely able to perform Roaring Aura Sky Ripping Fist, Bang wonders if monsterization is what allows Garou to make use of this devastating technique. Despite a grazing blow from Garou, the resulting shockwave was powerful enough to seemingly devastate Bang's body, ultimately leading to his defeat after a grueling battle. Though as strong as Roaring Aura Sky Ripping Fist is, Murata has still stated that it is inferior to Cross Fang Dragon Slayer Fist, another powerful technique that also combines Bang's and Bomb's martial arts.
Robots Robots (ロボット, "Robotto") are mechanical beings that are either remotely-controlled or have their own artificial intelligence.

Rosie Rosie (ロジー, "Rojī"; Viz: Rogy) was a martial artist and user of the Psycho Analysis Martial Arts. After eating Monster Cells, offered by Gouketsu, Rosie became a Mysterious Being and joined the Monster Association. He was killed by Choze. Appearance. Rosie was a young man with light-colored eyes and grey hair that parted to the left and had an undercut. He wore an Air Force Blue suit with a white shirt underneath and a red diamond-patterned tie. After eating the Monster Cells he grew more muscular and larger in size, and also had some protrusions sticking from his back. Personality. Rosie was very ambitious and planned to revolutionize psychology and logic in martial arts. Deep inside, he was a coward who was easily willing to do anything to survive, even if it meant abandoning his martial art style and his own humanity for the sake of surviving as he is the first one to rush to eat the Monster Cell. As a monster, he was quite vengeful and sadistic, as he beats a heavily injured Dave to avenge his humiliating defeat in the first round of the tournament. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Rosie is participating in the Super Fight Tournament in C-City at the C-City Super Stadium. This is the first time Rosie has participated in the tournament. While watching the match between Max and Suiryu, he was shocked by the strength of the latter, easily defeating his opponent. He was matched and defeated by Dave without much difficulty. Super Fight Arc. As he was being taken to the hospital, The Three Crows took him hostage and brought him back to the stadium, along with Dave and Bazuzu. Rosie and the martial artists were given an offer by Gouketsu, to either eat the Monster Cells and join the Monster Association, or die. Rosie was the first to eat it and after becoming a monster, he sadistically throws a heavily injured Dave into the distance to avenge his defeat in the tournament. However, his victory is short-lived as Choze quickly snaps his neck, killing him. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about Rosie's strength. Despite his strength as a monster, being able to knock around Dave who is considerably heavy, he was easily beaten by a human Choze. However, he seemed to have a decent amount of willpower as he did not lose his mind upon transformation. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: After becoming a monster, his strength increased to where he could toss Dave high into the sky with one arm. Enhanced Durability: In his human form, he survived being crushed by Dave with enough force to make a crater in the arena. Fighting Style. Psycho Analysis Martial Arts (心理分析格闘戦術, "Shinri Bunseki Kakutō Senjutsu"; Viz: Psychoanalytic Martial Arts): Not shown. He analyzes his foe's psychology and turns it in his favor. This style was actually useless in his first match in the Super Fight tournament since he was crushed by Dave in mere seconds before he could even react. It is worth noting, however, that since Dave's style is simply crushing people, it is possible it at least doesn't work on extremely simplistic styles like that one. Trivia. Rosie's name ロジー, "Rojī" is a pun on ロジック, "logic".

Royal Ripper Royal Ripper (キリサキング, "Kirisakingu"; Viz: King the Ripper) was a member of the Monster Association and an infamous Mysterious Being of urban legend. He was killed by Garou. Appearance. Royal Ripper was a humanoid monster wrapped almost completely in bandages, having exposed only his right eye and his long dark disheveled hair. Over his wrappings, he wore a worn-out tattered red dress and flat black shoes. Instead of hands, he had a pair of long and sharp straight blades that he sometimes used to scratch the floor in a menacing manner. Royal Ripper's inside was nothing like that of a normal human, but a mixture of hair, blood, and gauze. Personality. Royal Ripper was a sadistic monster with a very strong drive towards torture and killing. He was shown to get excited over cutting apart anyone, enemies and allies alike. He experienced intense sadism towards children, and Black Sperm was not surprised when Royal Ripper disappeared with Tareo, remarking that "He couldn't hold back his urges." Phoenix Man described him as an "a one-of-a-kind psycho who kills for pleasure," so much so that even other monsters avoided going anywhere near him. He even stated to Tareo that he didn't care for the Monster Association, as his only goal in life was to slaughter other creatures. He was very psychotic, yet childish, referring to his fellow monsters with honorifics in a rather playful manner. Although he enjoyed toying with his opponents, he could easily be overwhelmed by his killing instincts as shown when he attacked a distracted Garou from behind and continued to viciously slash at him despite the latter already being down. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Royal Ripper attempts to murder Narinki's Private Squad before Do-S stops him. Gyoro Gyoro later sends him and Bug God to watch and see if Garou can fulfill his mission assigned by Orochi. Royal Ripper confronts the Hero Hunter when he questioned whether he was truly a monster. As proof of Garou being a monster, Royal Ripper demanded Garou to murder Tareo. However, Royal Ripper's urges for killing children soon take over, ultimately resulting in Royal Ripper and Bug God fighting Garou. Despite the combined efforts of Royal Ripper and Bug God, Garou managed to fend them off. However, Sludge Jellyfish took Tareo hostage, distracting Garou and allowing Royal Ripper and Bug God to attack. After cutting Garou severely, Royal Ripper is stopped by Bug God. Believing Garou to be dead, Royal Ripper leaves with Bug God and Sludge Jellyfish, with Tareo as a captive. Royal Ripper takes Tareo to the Monster Association base and puts him in the same cell as Waganma. He tells the two to play nice, and momentarily leaves in order to regain his strength. He eventually returns to the cell and chooses Tareo to torture for his pleasure. After threatening the boy, he decides to begin the torture but is interrupted by Garou. Garou breaks through the wall and quickly kills Royal Ripper by punching off his head and using the Whirlwind Iron Cutting Fist to rip his body apart. After his death, his bandages are used by Garou to wrap his wounds up. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level threat, Royal Ripper was a powerful monster. While teaming up with Bug God, he was able to fight Garou for a considerable period of time and give him trouble. However, Garou stated that Royal Ripper was nowhere near as strong as Bang and the Hero Hunter still believed that he could have been able to defeat him. Royal Ripper also managed to put Garou in a near-death state, albeit the latter was caught off-guard and Royal Ripper himself was injured during the battle, as noted by Gyoro Gyoro. Physical Abilities. Immense Speed & Reflexes: Royal Ripper could swiftly kill the monsters attempting to attack Narinki's Private Squad. He was also capable of keeping up with Garou in combat, despite Garou himself possessing superhuman speed. Royal Ripper also managed to quickly sneak behind Garou while the Hero Hunter was distracted, and land a serious slash. Immense Strength: As a Demon-level Mysterious Being, Royal Ripper was very powerful. He was able to slash apart multiple monsters with his blades. Along with Bug God, he was capable of defeating and putting Garou in a near-death state, albeit with the help of a distraction. Enhanced Durability: Royal Ripper was able to take a direct kick from Garou in the stomach that knocked him away and recover in little time. Enhanced Senses: Royal Ripper was capable of smelling the presence of humans near him. Joint Reallocation: Royal Ripper has been shown to reallocate his joints to have movement with more degrees of freedom. This allowed him to move his blades more freely while making his blade arms less of an inconvenience. Fighting Style. Expert Swordsman: Royal Ripper was very skilled with the blades that were in the place of his hands. He demonstrated this by making multiple erratic slashes in combat.
Rules Rules may refer to:

Rumbling Thunder Rumbling Thunder (雷鳴のサンダー, "Raimei no Sandā") is a ninja from the Ninja Village. He is from the 37th graduating class, and a member of the Heavenly Ninja Party. Appearance. Rumbling Thunder had large, spiky hair and long sideburns. He wore a coat with fuzz along its cuffs and collar and a lightning bolt embroidered on the stomach. He also wore knee-length pants. Personality. Little is known about his personality, although it can be theorized that since he's part of the same graduating class as Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame, he takes great pride in his abilities and his class's reputation. He was the only one of the ninja who was not impressed by Sonic's Ten Shadow Burial, calling it a desperate struggle. Like the rest of the Heavenly Ninja Party, Rumbling Thunder despises Flashy Flash for destroying the village, showing he respects the village despite all of the harsh training it put him through. He also possesses a sense of comradery and joined together with the other ninjas of the village. History. Rumbling Thunder graduated from the 37th class of the Ninja Village, known as "Golden." This was the same class as Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame. He later joined the Heavenly Ninja Party. Abilities and Powers. As a graduate of the Ninja Village and a member of the Heavenly Ninja Party, Rumbling Thunder is a very powerful ninja. Furthermore, it can be assumed that since he is from the same class as Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame, the "Golden" class, his abilities exceed most of the other ninjas of the village and are on-par with Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame outside of their monster forms. He was the only one not impressed by Sonic's Ten Shadow Burial, and he, along with the other ninja, were easily able to take care of his clones. However, he was ultimately no match for Speed-o'-Sound Sonic and Flashy Flash, and was killed during their fight. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: As a graduate of the "Golden" class of the Ninja Village, Rumbling Thunder naturally has commendable strength. Immense Speed and Reflexes: As a graduate of the "Golden" class of the Ninja Village, Rumbling Thunder possesses amazing speed and reflexes, being able to trade blows with Flashy Flash and stop Sonic's clones, although he was unable to react to having his arm sliced off and shurikens thrown at him by Sonic.

Rumored Monster Arc The Rumored Monster Arc is the fifth arc of the "One-Punch Man" series, and the second arc of the Hero Association Saga. Plot. The Hero Association staff are having a meeting, discussing reports from various cities. The association sends Spring Mustachio and Golden Ball to investigate rumors about the abandoned section of Z-City. They encounter Kombu Infinity, who defeats them. The monster informs them that it isn't the rumored monster, but seeks to become the monster for fun. It encounters Saitama, who steals its kombu hair to make soup. Genos believes Saitama is trying to regrow his hair with the kombu, but Saitama firmly denies it.

Ryumon Ryumon (リュウモン, "Ryūmon") is a hero for the Neo Heroes. He is also the leader of the gangster organization Ryumon Gang. Appearance. Ryumon has the appearance of a battle-worn gangster. He has dark, slicked back hair that is shaved on the sides, as well as thick eyebrows and sunken eyes. He is missing his front teeth and has 3 lines of stitches running from his mouth down his jaw. He wears a fancy jacket with fur trim on the collar and cuffs, as well as black gloves and several chains around his neck. His eyes are also large with lots of lines under them. The lines give him a battle-worn appearance. Personality. Ryumon is excited about the Neo Heroes betting system allowing people to bet on the monsters too. Ryumon presents himself as a well-mannered man seeking to redeem himself from his past actions as a gangster, but has expressed his wishes to carry weapons in public. As a result, Accel suspects that he is merely putting up a facade. Plot. McCoy calls Ryumon and thanks him for advising on plans to bring down the Hero Association. Neo Heroes Saga. Supreme Hero Arc. Prior to the official Neo Heroes leader meeting, Ryumon is seen asking if he can use his hero status to openly carry firearms. During the meeting, he states that he and his gang have reformed themselves, but Accel is skeptical of this claim. When the tiger-level Triple Tongues attack, Ryumon and his group step in, saving Crescent Eyebroll. Eyebroll offers to help, but Ryumon brushes off his help, calling him small fry and mocking the Hero Association. The members of the Ryumon Gang then attack Triple Tongues, stating that the monsters' attacks don't hurt at all. Abilities and Powers. Given that Ryumon is the head of the 400-member strong Ryumon Gang and one of the top members of the Neo Heroes, it can be assumed that he is a powerful individual. Additionally, his interest in weapons indicates that he could be adept in using them, particularly firearms.
Ryumon Gang Ryumon Gumi (リュウモン組, "Ryūmon-gumi") is a gangster organisation led by Ryumon. It consists of 400 members. They are allied with the Neo Heroes.

S-City S-City (S市, S" Shi") is a city on Earth. There are 31 heroes living in this city. Locations. Garou's Hideout. A shack located in the forest in a park where Garou usually rested in after his battles. Mouse Sushi. Mouse Sushi is a popular sushi restaurant. Saitama, Narinki, Waganma and Bad have all eaten there. S-City Nature Park. A public nature park in S-City. Garou took shelter in the park in between hunts. The park is incredibly large, even larger than Elder Centipede. Cafe & Restaurant Togus. The cafe is visited by Garou, Saitama and Fubuki. They serve a variety western food. Inhabitants. Heroes. Number of Heroes by Class: Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Junior Centipede and Venus Mantrap emerge from underneath the Mouse Sushi restaurant to kidnap a sponsor of the Hero Association, but they are stopped by Metal Bat. After defeating Junior Centipede and Venus Mantrap, Metal Bat is faced with fighting two Demon level monsters; Senior Centipede, and Rafflesidon. The city is set on high alert during this battle. After the defeat of the Demon level monsters, Elder Centipede emerges and wreaks havoc throughout the city. Citizens are alerted to evacuate the city as fast as possible. Elder Centipede flings Bad across the city. Garou shows up and fights Metal Bat to a draw after Zenko interrupts the battle. Metal Bat then collapses from exhaustion. Monster Association Arc. Garou returns to the city to rest but is pursued by waves of heroes until the Monster Association comes to his rescue. Elder Centipede emerges once again and begins spreading destruction. However, the centipede monster is ultimately destroyed by Saitama later.

Sage Centipede Sage Centipede (ムカデ, "Mukade Sen'nin"; Viz: Centisennin) is an immensely large centipede-like Mysterious Being. It claims to have emerged to destroy "The Abominable Fist That Has Turned Against God". It was killed by Garou. Appearance. Sage Centipede is a massive centipede-like creature, surpassing even Elder Centipede who was already one of the largest monsters seen. While it does bear some resemblance to Elder Centipede, it is notably more monstrous to a degree, having a sharper and spiky armor that sticks out. Its mandibles are also bigger while its antennas are wider and thicker. According to Sage Centipede itself, its limbs are 6666 in total, and look like twisted humanoid arms with claws and armor on them. It appears to have three faces - Its "normal" centipede face with two eyes, a dragon-like face between the eyes which has two main eyes with two smaller eyes behind each one, and a humanoid skull-like third face with five eyes and no lower jaw on the second face's forehead. Sage Centipede is so long that it could extend from ground to space. Personality. Sage Centipede portrays itself as a single-minded being, bent on achieving the singular goal of destroying "The Abominable Fist That Has Turned Against God" (later revealed to be Saitama). As such, it boasts of its superiority in the face of humanity, thinking of humans as insolent and tiny. Extremely aggressive and powerful, Sage Centipede threatened to execute "divine retribution and destruction" for the sake of the Earth, whom it acknowledges as "father", as well as proclaiming the planet's oceans as "mother". During the fight with Garou and Metal Bat, Sage Centipede displays its cowardly nature on more than one occasion by taking a helicopter hostage, which has Tareo and some heroes inside. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Sage Centipede is first seen deep beneath the Earth where the Mysterious Shrine was located, only with its shadow rising. Later on, after Garou defeats Platinum Sperm, Sage Centipede bursts out from the massive hole where Tatsumaki has attacked Orochi. After making its appearance, Sage Centipede loudly claims that it has been sent to destroy "The Abominable Fist That Has Turned Against God" and declares itself the "Incarnation of Father Earth". As Sage Centipede directs its eyes towards the sea, Evil Natural Water, now known as Evil Ocean Water, begins rising. Sage Centipede refers to Evil Ocean Water as the "Incarnation of Mother Ocean", stating that along with the latter, it will bring total destruction. In an instant, Garou jumps up towards Sage Centipede and pummels it in the head. Sage Centipede takes damage from Garou's attack. However it quickly regenerates, and despite Garou's attempts to grab its attention, Sage Centipede realizes Garou seemed concerned about the rescue helicopter (which Tareo is inside) behind it. It tells Garou if he moves an inch, Evil Ocean Water will shoot down the helicopter instantly. While Garou is surprised, Sage Centipede attacks him with its Centipede Grand March, with Evil Ocean Water aiding the giant centipede by shooting a devastating water cannon at him, severely injuring the Hero Hunter. Despite the successful attack though, Sage Centipede notices unknown movement from Saitama who dashes towards and punches Evil Ocean Water, shocking Sage Centipede at the immense damage done and pondering if Evil Ocean Water's supposed death was caused by a tectonic shift. As the rescue helicopter in the sky seems to bother Sage Centipede, it targets and attempts to strike down the flying object. At this moment, Metal Bat from nearby, jumps towards its humanoid face and strikes it with many direct swings, although Sage Centipede remains practically unharmed and simply tosses the S-Class hero away. Sage Centipede continues its attempts to strike down the rescue helicopter, but a reporter helicopter pops up right above it, much to its annoyance. Sage Centipede then strikes the reporter helicopter with one of its antennas. However, Metal Bat manages to appear in front of the helicopter and blocks the strike. Shortly after Garou, already recovered from the damage he sustained earlier, lands a barrage of attacks on Sage Centipede, which momentarily knock back the giant monster but do not cause any serious damage to it. After an argument between Garou and Metal Bat, they soon team up to defeat Sage Centipede. Despite the two of them attacking all across its body, Sage Centipede still shrugs off their assault thanks to its toughness plus with its excellent regenerative abilities. Although Sage Centipede considers Garou a threat, he does not think the same for Metal Bat and while thinking of using the latter as a hostage, seeing the two argue makes the giant monster give up that idea. Sage Centipede continues to pursue the helicopter, which Tareo and the wounded heroes are inside, in an attempt to take the plane hostage. When the monster comes very close, One Shotter shoots it in the head but misses. Sage Centipede eventually catches the helicopter with its antennas, shattering the rotor and taking the people inside hostages. At this moment, Garou and Metal Bat both stop dead in their tracks, which prompts Sage Centipede to attack the two with its Centipede Grand March, causing the entire terrain to change shape and seemingly taking down them. Sage Centipede then grabs an injured Garou, who is on his knees, with one of its human arms. Just as Sage Centipede is about to finish off the Human Monster, One Shotter, now able to aim accurately thanks to having support from Gearsper, shoots the monster multiple times at its eyes, momentarily distracting it and allowing Garou to pry open the hold and escape. Immediately after, Garou pummels Sage Centipede and attempts to free the helicopter from the monster's antennas. Sage Centipede soon tries to attack Garou with its mandibles but Metal Bat appears and chops off Sage Centipede's antennas, much to its surprise.
