After Puri-Puri Prisoner's explanation, Baquma proceeds to bombard him with multiple attacks using the powers he had absorbed from those monsters earlier. Baquma is amazed that Puri-Puri Prisoner is still standing even after taking those attacks, viewing him as a monster, although he notices that the hero's body is beginning to tremble from the pain of the venom and electric shocks. Baquma claims that while Puri-Puri Prisoner's spirit is strong, his body however can't keep up. Suddenly, Puri-Puri Prisoner touches a stone wall with his vibrating finger, and the entire wall gets pulverised from the excessive vibrations. Baquma is shocked, and asks him what did he just do. The S-Class hero replies by saying his love has managed to give birth to a brand new fighting style: Vibration ☆ Angel. Puri-Puri Prisoner unleashes his new attack: Vibration Dark ☆ Angel ☆ Rush, and rushes toward Baquma. The monster's final thoughts are that Puri-Puri Prisoner really is a monster, and he is utterly decimated by Puri-Puri Prisoner's attack, making Puri-Puri Prisoner the victor.

Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Deep Sea King Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Deep Sea King is the battle between the S-Class hero Puri-Puri Prisoner and Deep Sea King, a Demon-level mysterious being. Prelude. After seeing Stinger struggling to defeat the Seafolk, Puri-Puri Prisoner breaks out of prison with Speed-o'-Sound Sonic in tow. Sonic thanks Puri-Puri Prisoner for breaking out and allowing him to escape. Puri-Puri Prisoner says Sonic's cell name and his actual name, which slightly surprises Sonic. Then, Deep Sea King arrives on the scene, remarking at how more soldiers have arrived to challenge him. Battle. As Deep Sea King arrives at the scene, Puri-Puri Prisoner remarks on how he can feel strength radiating from Deep Sea King. He shortly monologues about his status as the lowest ranked S-Class hero, but an S-Class hero nonetheless. He chooses to battle at 50% power, then bulks up his muscles, which causes him to unintentionally rips his boyfriend's sweater. Puri-Puri Prisoner shouts in agony, lamenting the loss of his sweater that his boyfriend knitted for him, and he declares he will never forgive the bastard monster who did it, even though it was Puri-Puri Prisoner's own fault. Deep Sea King licks his lips, and remarks how delectable and prime the fresh meat standing before him is, claiming he has wet his appetite, and throws a heavy right punch at Puri-Puri Prisoner. The S-Class hero retaliates with a punch of his own, sending the monster flying a short distance. Both taunt their opponent's attacks, saying they felt it just a little. However, Sonic detects that it was Puri-Puri Prisoner who took more damage, and that he is simply bluffing. Puri-Puri Prisoner realizes he will have to go all out in order to spare anyone else from Deep Sea King's wrath, and transforms into his signature Angel ☆ Style. As Sonic watches, he is slightly disgusted at Puri-Puri Prisoner's naked body, saying he is definitely not an angel, nor is he human. The S-Class hero states that nobody has seen his Angel ☆ Style and walked away alive, then lunges at Deep Sea King, sending a barrage of punches with his Angel ☆ Rush attack, as smoke clouds arise in the process. As the smoke clears, Deep Sea King looks almost completely unfazed, to the shock of both Puri-Puri Prisoner and Sonic. Deep Sea King belittles Puri-Puri Prisoner by saying he felt that as well, but only a little. Deep Sea King then lands a series of powerful blows to Puri-Puri Prisoner, to which he is unable to defend against. Just before he delivers the final combo attack, Deep Sea King heeds some words of advice to the S-Class hero and tells him the purpose of a combo attack is to finish off your opponent, meaning each attack must be delivered with the intent to kill. Deep Sea King then brutalizes the S-Class hero with a seemingly endless barrage of punches, sending the hero crashing through a nearby building and ending the battle with Deep Sea King as the victor. Aftermath. This battle seriously affects Puri-Puri Prisoner, and the newspapers dub him an S-Class failure. From this battle, however, Puri-Puri Prisoner takes Deep Sea King's advice, and creates his latest and most powerful combo attack: Dark ☆ Angel ☆ Rush, that he uses against Melzargard later on.

Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Free Hugger Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Free Hugger was the fight between the S-Class hero Puri-Puri Prisoner and the Demon-level mysterious being Free Hugger of the Monster Association. Prelude. Free Hugger is one of several monsters sent to create chaos in the cities by the Monster Association. Puri-Puri Prisoner is informed of Free Hugger and is sent to kill the monster. When the hero finds Free Hugger, the two engage in battle. Battle. An off-screen battle takes place, but during the beginning of the battle, Puri-Puri Prisoner is at a great disadvantage. Due to Free Hugger's spiked body and his hand-to-hand combat style, Puri-Puri Prisoner sustains several deep cuts and wounds all across his body, while Free Hugger remains practically unharmed. Puri-Puri Prisoner feels very concerned about the situation, stating that he can't use his full power with the damage he's sustained and he cannot damage Free Hugger without inflicting greater harm on himself. From the sidelines, several citizens are watching this battle, worrying that if an S-Class hero is having trouble with this opponent, the monster must indeed be tough. Another citizen notes that he's having a tough time because he's fighting barehanded. They then notice the iron ball chained around Puri-Puri Prisoner's foot, and yell at the hero to use that as a weapon. Puri-Puri Prisoner hears them shouting at him and thanks them for their fervent support, not hearing what they're actually trying to tell him. The spectators realize this and are disappointed, while one of the spectators finds it uncomfortable that he is fighting naked. The hero is grateful for their support regardless of the possible danger, and says that their unbridled love will not go to waste. Suddenly, Puri-Puri Prisoner comes to the realization that in order to escape this ordeal, he must accept all of the pain with deep, overflowing love. With this epiphany, he no longer fears the pain of Free Hugger's spiked body and proceeds to trap the monster with his Angel ☆ Hug, crushing the monster and making Puri-Puri Prisoner the victor. Aftermath. Puri-Puri Prisoner is pleased with this victory, but the spectators are unnerved by Puri-Puri Prisoner's bizarre nature and fear that the hero is becoming enamored with them. But then, Puri-Puri Prisoner gets a phone call informing him that his homies in Smelly Lid Prison have gone missing, and destroys his phone in anger. Quickly after, Saitama comes across Free Hugger's corpse while running throughout the city trying to find any monsters that may have still been roaming.

Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Nyan Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Nyan was the fight between the S-Class hero Puri-Puri Prisoner and the Monster Association executive Nyan. Prelude. While the prisoners of Smelly Lid Prison attack Puri-Puri Prisoner, Nyan comes in from behind the hero. Nyan tells him that once someone becomes a monster, they can never go back. Battle. Before Puri-Puri Prisoner can even react, Nyan slashes the hero across his chest with minimal effort, yawning in the process. He attacks the hero again with his Feline Retribution, drawing up large portions of blood and ripping Puri-Puri Prisoner's sweater apart. As Puri-Puri Prisoner evolves during the battle and attempts to forcibly shower the prisoners with love, Nyan begins to feel uneasy. This is because he was once a house cat, and his former master would constantly shower him with unwanted love. Not wanting to deal with a similar foe, the monstrous cat decides to retreat and manages to slip through the crack in the wall. Puri-Puri Prisoner does not understand how Nyan could do this, and the monster replies by saying he can pass through any gap larger than 3 millimeters, and since there are so many cracks, he can easily travel around the Monster Association Headquarters. Despite his retreat, Puri-Puri Prisoner does not allow Nyan to run away like this, and so he decides to increase the power of his vibration with his bristle armor on his forearms. The hero dives into the concrete like a swimmer and uses his Angel ☆ Crawl to chase after Nyan. Nyan notices this and enters another crack in an attempt to lose the hero. Alas, Puri-Puri Prisoner is still determined to chase him to the ends of the Earth and catches up with Nyan. They come across the prisoners again, with one of them asking Nyan if he killed Puri-Puri Prisoner. From above, Puri-Puri Prisoner comes crashing down, and he accidentally crushes the prisoners and kills them with his Angel ☆ Crawl. Puri-Puri Prisoner mourns the death of his fellow prisoners, but quickly focuses his attention on Nyan and prepares to fight the Dragon-level monster and avenge the deaths of the prisoners. However, by this point, Nyan has already retreated outside of Puri-Puri Prisoner's vision, going to search for other heroes to fight. Puri-Puri Prisoner does not get this, however, because he is the weakest of the S-Class heroes, and as he walks through the headquarters to search for more monsters, he states that Nyan will regret fighting whichever hero he comes across next. Aftermath. After Nyan retreats through the cracks of the headquarters, he comes across Saitama and attempts to strike him with a surprise attack. However, he is shocked to realize the attack had no effect, and immediately retreats again.

Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Prisoners of Smelly Lid Prison Puri-Puri Prisoner vs. Prisoners of Smelly Lid Prison was the battle between the S-Class hero Puri-Puri Prisoner and the monsterized prisoners of Smelly Lid Prison. Prelude. As Puri-Puri Prisoner destroys Baquma, the prisoners of Smelly Lid Prison walk onto the scene talking about how Puri-Puri Prisoner should be considered a monster, and their failed attempts to kill him because of his physical prowess. The monsters eagerly prepare their revenge and declare the hero as their sworn enemy. Puri-Puri Prisoner recognizes those voices and is shocked that the captured prisoners were transformed into monsters. He claims to be sickened that they monsterized such weak men, enraging the monsters for calling them weak and causing them to charge at the hero. Battle. As they all blitz Puri-Puri Prisoner, each of them talks about the punishment they endured in their prison. One of them says they will go back to the prison and kill the guards, while another says that the Deep Sea Kiss punishment was absolutely unforgivable, adding onto this by saying they would have been legendary serial killers if it wasn't for him. Puri-Puri Prisoner is saddened that the prisoners had their hearts corrupted after becoming monsters, although the prisoners assure him that they have always hated his guts. Puri-Puri Prisoner is shocked by this, and tells them to remember all of the memories they made together. Unfortunately, the prisoners are not moved, causing Puri-Puri Prisoner to tear up, as he still loves the prisoners and is determined to save them. Then, out of nowhere, a monster appears from behind Puri-Puri Prisoner and tells him that once someone becomes a monster, they can never go back. This monster is revealed to be Nyan, and before Puri-Puri Prisoner can even react, Nyan slashes the hero across his chest with minimal effort, yawning in the process. He attacks the hero again with his Feline Retribution, drawing up large portions of blood and ripping Puri-Puri Prisoner's sweater apart. The prisoners are amazed by Nyan's power and rush Puri-Puri Prisoner while he is distracted, but the hero gets back up and tells the monsters that as long as they have a human heart, they will always be fine humans. He continues by proclaiming that he will rescue his boyfriends, and that with love, nothing is impossible. The prisoners are shocked that their words are still not getting through to him, and they attack him once again, although this time, he does not attempt to defend himself and takes the attacks with no damage. Nyan notices this, and realizes that the accumulated damage awakened his defensive instincts, and his body is adapting rapidly as a result. At first, Puri-Puri Prisoner wonders if he grew angel wings, but one of the prisoners tells him it's just body hair, which has improved his defenses. The hero calls this new defense Angel ☆ Bristle Armor, and with his heightened defenses, decides to attack Nyan, since the attacks from the prisoners now do no damage to him. Surprisingly, Nyan does not attack, but instead, begins to feel dread creeping up his spine. This is because he was once a house cat, and his former master would constantly shower him with unwanted love. Not wanting to deal with a similar foe, the monstrous cat decides to retreat and manages to slip through the crack in the wall. Puri-Puri Prisoner does not understand how Nyan could do this, and the monster replies by saying he can pass through any gap larger than 3 millimeters, and since there are so many cracks, he can easily travel around the Monster Association Headquarters. Despite his retreat, Puri-Puri Prisoner does not allow Nyan to run away like this, and so he decides to increase the power of his vibration with his bristle armor on his forearms. The hero dives into the concrete like a swimmer and uses his Angel ☆ Crawl to chase after Nyan. Nyan notices this and enters another crack in an attempt to lose the hero. Alas, Puri-Puri Prisoner is still determined to chase him to the ends of the Earth and catches up with Nyan. They come across the prisoners again, with one of them asking Nyan if he killed Puri-Puri Prisoner. From above, Puri-Puri Prisoner comes crashing down, and he accidentally crushes the prisoners and kills them with his Angel ☆ Crawl. He sees this and falls to the ground, agonizing over their deaths with tears in his eyes. Aftermath. Puri-Puri Prisoner quickly recovers from the grief of their losses, using his anguish as rage to use against Nyan. He accepts his new technique as a gift from all of them and thanks them, while the body hair falls off of his body. The hero declares their deaths will not be in vain, and he prepares to eliminate Nyan, while one of the prisoner's last thoughts is cursing at him before he succumbs to death.

Q-City Q-City (Q市 "Q Shi") is a large city situated on the Earth. Not much is known about the location, other than the hero in charge of supervision of the city is the S-Class, Watchdog Man. Q-City is labeled as the most dangerous city in terms of number and average disaster level of Mysterious Beings. However, Watchdog Man seems to be keeping the area calm. Civilians clean the monster remains after the battles by Watchdog Man. There are 13 heroes living in this city. Locations. Watchdog Plaza. Watchdog Plaza is a famous meeting point where many fans go to take pictures. The plaza has an observation platform for Watchdog Man. Inhabitants. Heroes. Number of Heroes by Class: Plot. Hero Association Saga. Rumored Monster Arc. The city is briefly seen when the Hero Association meeting discussing the status reports from various cities is shown. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Garou comes to Q-City to challenge Watchdog Man to a fight. However, various monsters from the Monster Association attempt to invade the city first, but Watchdog Man easily crushes the invasion, letting Garou see Watchdog Man's fighting style first hand. Super Fight Arc. After Watchdog Man kills all the monsters, Garou charges at him but is easily defeated by the hero.

R-City R-City (R市 "R Shi") is a large city situated on the Earth. There are 14 heroes living in this city. Locations. Major Talent Company: Handsome Castle. The Handsome Castle is a talent company where newcomer celebrities come. Sweet Mask is the main face of the talent agency and the Soda Pop Boys are a group of wanna-be heroes that recently joined the Hero Association. Inhabitants. Heroes. Number of Heroes by Class: Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. Sweet Mask gets introduced to the Soda Pop Boys and is asked to take them under his guidance. He rejects the idea and insults the group, calling them copycats and an "ugly imitation" of him. Cherion, a member of the group and a C-Class hero, challenges Sweet Mask, but suddenly feels a shivering chill when he sees Sweet Mask's veiny neck and face.

Rabbit Rabbit (ラビット, "Rabitto") is a C-Class hero employed by the Hero Association. Appearance. Rabbit is a young man with black hair. He wears a bunny outfit, making him look like an anthropomorphic rabbit, along with bunny ears and a pair of sunglasses. Personality. Rabbit is a rather emotionless individual with little character, which is why he chose to put on his rabbit costume in order to make himself appear more eccentric. History. At some point, he became employed by the Hero Association. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Rabbit, Hacker Net, Meat Pounder and are seen wandering in W-City worried over the monster raid on the city. Zombieman steps in and assures their fears as he deals with the monster Marshall Gorilla. Zombieman tells Rabbit and the others to help the wounded and look for the remaining monsters. Power and Abilities. As a C-Class hero, it can be assumed that Rabbit is a rather weak hero. He used to be a stressed-out salaryman and he barely passed the pro-hero exam. As he lacked personality, he put on a costume.

Rafflesidon Rafflesidon (ラフレシドン, "Rafureshidon"; Viz: Lafreshidon) was a Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. He was killed by Metal Bat. Appearance. Rafflesidon bore a great resemblance to the Rafflesia flower albeit with slightly more rounded features. However, despite his great resemblance to the flower, he had two eyes with completely black sclera and white irises. He had a bulbous nose with a wood like texture to it. He also had many of his roots sticking out in several directions. Personality. Rafflesidon took a calculated approach in battle, relying on others to distract an opponent while he releases gases to manipulate the battleground. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. After Senior Centipede knocks Metal Bat, Narinki, and Waganma out of the restaurant, Rafflesidon releases his Hypno Scent and emerges from the sewers. Narinki and Waganma immediately fall unconscious. Rafflesidon and Senior Centipede are left to fight Metal Bat. While Senior Centipede and Rafflesidon fight Metal Bat, Rafflesidon is able to get Metal Bat into a hypnotic state. However, Metal Bat eventually pulls himself out of the hypnotic state by bonking his head and kills Rafflesidon with a single strike. Abilities and Powers. Physical Abilities. Gas Release: Rafflesidon had the ability to release a sleeping gas that induces unconsciousness after inhalation. Fighting Style. Hypno Scent (催眠香, "Saimin Kō"): Rafflesidon releases a gas that puts a target to sleep. A stronger human like Metal Bat can resist the effects of the gas for longer, but given enough exposure will still succumb to its sleep-inducing effects. Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Despite mainly being a supporting role in battle, Rafflesidon was still decently skilled in close-quarters combat and would engage in such scenarios with his vines.

Raiden Raiden (ライデン, "Raiden") is a Super Sumo champion, formerly holding the rank of "yokozuna". He works as a hero for the Neo Heroes. Appearance. Raiden is an extremely large and muscular man with black hair and dark eyes. He sports the traditional appearance, complete with a white and a topknot haircut. Personality. Raiden is adamant about not joining the current Hero Association. He instead gets contracted with the Neo Heroes. Raiden is very confident about his strength, boasting about his legendary reputation and challenging Superalloy Darkshine to a sparring match. Similar to Darkshine, he has the desire to fight strong opponents, and after seeing how scared Darkshine was after attempting to fight him, internally wondered if Darkshine was past his prime, disappointing him. He also seems to have an honorable and compassionate side however. As shown when he called off the spar because he noticed that Darkshine wasn't in proper fighting condition and didn't want to intimidate him. He also expressed some concern for Darkshine's safety, warning him to get out of the way when Mars Leo was going on a rampage. He believes that great strength through hard training is always better than any scientific modification on a human body since he thinks that body enhancement restricts the latent ability of the human body. Despite this, he seems to have a cruel demeanor towards criminals, preferring to forcibly turn them into mind-controlled cyborgs as opposed to more humane means of prison reform. He appears to have had a change of heart after fighting Puri-Puri Prisoner, viewing him as a true hero and vowing to keep an open mind towards his reformative justice. Raiden also holds great conviction in his values, being willing to directly defy his leader's orders when he thinks they aren't just. History. When he was an active professional Super Sumo wrestler, Raiden fought and won 700 consecutive fights, becoming the Super Sumo Yokozuna and gaining a reputation as the strongest wrestler of all time. As a child he was a natural prodigy, having never lost a single fight or sports competition, even if he was facing adults. Because of his incredible strength, he was visited by scouts sent by the Hero Association multiple times, with the request to join them and work as a professional S-Class Hero. He refused all their offers. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Introduction Arc. Raiden was once again approached by a Hero Association scout with yet another offer to join their ranks, but the yokozuna yet again refused their offer. This time Raiden revealed to the scout that he was already contracted with the newly-founded Neo Heroes. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Raiden is later seen at a Neo Heroes meeting, having been given the prestigious position of Neo Leader. Suiryu is introduced to Raiden and the others, and Raiden briefly grapples with Superalloy Darkshine to test his strength. During a monster invasion, Raiden saves another hero by palm striking a monster and stepping on another, killing them both. He then questions the power of the Neo Heroes Battle Suits, stating that they're not necessary for someone like him. Raiden is later seen testing a battle suit, and he has a flashback to the reason for wearing one. It is revealed that Raiden had fought Puri-Puri Prisoner, and although he landed multiple heavy blows and took no damage, he was ultimately unable to incapacitate to the S-Class hero due to his pain suppression. Eventually realizing that Puri-Puri Prisoner is focused on protecting his prisoners and not fighting back, he realizes that he is actually a hero despite his odd sense of justice. Raiden then walks away declaring that he will tell his leader that Puri-Puri Prisoner is a hero. Jumping back to the present, Raiden continues to think about how he was able to find out the power of an S-Class hero himself, however he questions how someone of Puri-Puri Prisoner's strength can be considered to be the weakest of the S-Class. After then pondering about how Superalloy Darkshine's spirit can be worn out from fighting evil, he declares that as a sumo his spirit will not falter and that now he is in a battle suit, he is ready for everything. Abilities and Powers. Raiden is known to have a "strength that surpasses knowledge", prompting the Hero Association to repeatedly invite him to join them as an S-Class Hero. His strength has also given him a reputation for having a body that goes beyond the realm of hominidae and grants him an overwhelming advantage over all biological beings. One time while Raiden was on vacation, he swatted a large monster to death with his bare hand. McCoy stated that in terms of battle prowess, Raiden is at the top of the class. The Neo Heroes' assessment of him suggests that his strength apparently even surpasses that of the Hero Association's S-Class level. Raiden momentarily grappled with Superalloy Darkshine, but Darkshine wasn't in proper fighting condition at the time. During his brief grapple with Darkshine, they shattered the ground beneath them. Raiden was able to exchange blows with Puri-Puri Prisoner, covering his body in blood and bruises while he remained unharmed. However, due to Puri-Puri Prisoner's new technique and pain suppression, he would not succumb to the damage Raiden was giving him. Raiden was confident that he'd beat Puri-Puri Prisoner, but decided to back down out of respect for his conviction. Despite his initial hesitance, Raiden is now using on the Neo Heroes strength augmenting suit. With this suit, he can effortlessly put huge craters into reinforced concrete, and make footsteps with enough force to cause tremors throughout an entire skyscraper. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: As the strongest Neo Hero in terms of battle prowess, Raiden has very impressive strength. His remarkable strength is shown when he decapitates a monster with just a casual palm strike and splits another monster in half by merely stepping on it. He also momentarily grappled with Superalloy Darkshine, the force creating fissures beneath them. Raiden's strength was immense enough to cause Darkshine to panic and sweat, though it should be noted that Darkshine was not in his best mindset. He was also able to damage Puri-Puri Prisoner in their fight, though he was ultimately unable to incapacitate the hero and both of them eventually stood down. Fighting Style. Sumo Wrestling: Raiden is a master sumo wrestler and the champion of Super Sumo, a style of sumo in which you have to be over 300 cm and 400 kg to be allowed to compete in. Since beginning his career as a Super Sumo wrestler, he's fought 700 matches and never lost a single time, demonstrating his impressive mastery of the art of sumo. Many of Raiden's strikes consist of palm strikes as opposed to punches.

Rangor Rangor (ランゴール, "Rangōru"; Viz: Langor) was one of the nine warriors of the Dragon Alliance. Appearance. Rangor is a very large and muscular figure. He is able to transform into a monstrous monster. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Introduction Arc. Rangor's goal was to steal one of the sealing orbs from The Saints so that he could summon the Cruel Dragon, but was killed by Saitama in one punch before he could do so. Abilities and Powers. Little is known about Rangor's strength due to how quickly Saitama killed him. He possesses the ability to transform into a monstrous state to increase his strength.

Raptora Raptora (ラプトラ, "Raputora") was a Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. She is the younger sister of Reptera. Appearance. Raptora is a female humanoid with reptilian attributes such as a tail, scales, and sharp teeth. Her figure is buxom. Her fair hair is tousled at the back and has two small braids next to her ears. A black collar with metallic tips adorns her neck. There are two black-tipped white twisted horns on its skull. Her outfit consists of a bra, black double-strap panties, as well as black heeled boots and black gloves with spikes. Raptora has two small earrings. She is armed with a cleaver coated with her venom. Personality. Raptora is a monster that has no mercy for humans and heroes. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Raptora, alongside some other Monster Association members, are guarding Waganma when Child Emperor infiltrates the prison cells of the organization. She and those fellow members are then gassed by the S-Class hero while he is trying to save Waganma. Abilities & Powers. Supernatural Abilities. Poison Manipulation: As a poison-based Mysterious Being, Raptora has the ability to produce poison. Equipment. Machete: Raptora wields a small machete in combat.

Ray Ray (レイ, "Rei") is a Machine God (機神, "Kishin") battle robot created by The Organization. It was destroyed by Genos. Appearance. Ray is a fairly tall humanoid robot with a masculine frame. Its head is covered in electric coils, and its face consists of a dark visor with three glowing eyes within. Its arms possess gatling gun-like cannons and it wears a cape-like loincloth around its waist. Personality. Ray is an analytical and methodical individual. During its fight with Genos, it constantly detected all of the hero's attacks, abilities, and changed in power and advised its comrades on the countermeasures against the cyborg's tactics. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Ray attacks Dr. Kuseno's laboratory alongside its comrades, Body and Tech. Their strike killed the doctor, throwing Genos into a rage. After Body struggles against Genos, the three robots decide to take him on together, with Ray remaining in the back to provide support with its cannons. However, Ray is still destroyed by a precise blow from Genos. Abilities and Powers. As a Dragon-level threat of the Organization, Ray is a very powerful Mysterious Being. Alongside its partners, Ray was capable of pressuring Genos even with his new upgrades, forcing the cyborg to use his last resort to keep up. Robotic Abilities. Immense Strength: As a Machine God, Ray presumably has remarkable strength, though given its preference to engage in long-range combat, it can be assumed that its physical strength is less in comparison to its comrades such as Body. Flight: Ray is capable of using boosters underneath its feet to hover in the air. Energy Projection: Ray is able to unleash energy bullets from its arms and even its head. Fighting Style. Unlike its comrades, who specialized in close-range combat, Ray preferred to utilize long-range combat, giving support fire while the others engaged their opponent in close quarters.

Reality Punch Reality Punch (現実パンチ, "Genjitsu Panchi") is an extra chapter included with Volume 19. Summary. Saitama is walking in Z-City reading a manga, thinking about the hero's journey, finishing moves, and hypothetical monsters. While wandering, Saitama encounters The Three Tempest Brothers. The monsters are annoyed by Saitama's obliviousness to their presence, but after Saitama easily kills one of them, the other 2 run back home.

Reanimation Reanimation is the ability to reanimate and command corpses and dead beings. Overview. This ability is extremely rare and useful, as it can resurrect any living thing back from the dead. So far, the only character that shown to possess this ability is Phoenix Man and there appears to be no limit as to how many individuals can be reanimated by him, as an army of hundreds of Subterraneans were reanimated to attack Brave Giant. Apparently, the reanimated corpses can also regain their sanity and cognitive functions if they receive a powerful enough shock, snapping them out of the puppeteer's control, as seen with Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame.

Reclusamurai Reclusamurai (引きこも侍, "Hikikomo-samurai") is the B-Class Rank 39 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. Reclusamurai wears a sandogasa and a karate gi. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Introduction Arc. Reclusamurai, Magic Trick Man, Dynamite Man, and Ecolo G attempt to defeat the Forest Tribe. They are nearly killed by the Forest King before being saved by Genos. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Sense. Reclusamurai is one of the contestants of the Hero Costume Contest under the entry number 7. Abilities and Powers. As a B-Class hero, it can be assumed that Reclusamurai is a fairly skilled combatant. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Senses: Reclusamurai can sense the distance between him and his opponent. He developed these senses by secluding himself in a small room for ten years. The range of this ability is very small. Equipment. Katana: Reclusamurai carries two katanas with round cross-guards.

Recollection Of A Most Sincere Apprentice "Recollection Of A Most Sincere Apprentice" (一番弟子の回想, "Ichibandeshi no Kaisou") is an extra chapter included with Volume 7. Summary. This chapter follows Charanko, as he is about to leave Bang's dojo. Charanko joined one year prior, in order to become popular with girls. Because Charanko is not a very good martial artist, he has always done all the chores in the dojo, and was frightened of his Senior, he also has not become any stronger or popular, so he decided to quit. When Charanko arrived at the door, he was surprised to find his master cleaning the floors, when he asked him why, he was told the others have all quit. Learning he was the only disciple left, he came to a realization that he is now the number one disciple, and so he decided to stay and work even harder.

Red Muffler Red Muffler (マフ, "Aka Mafu") is the C-Class Rank 89 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. Red Muffler is a young man with short light-colored hair. He wears armor featuring a chest plate, shoulder pads and shin guards with a star on the chest plate and shoulder pads. He also wears a large red scarf around his neck. Personality. Red Muffler is a realistic young man, and understands the limits of his abilities. History. Cicida Larva Attack. Red Muffler attempted to fight the 170,000-Year-Old Cicada Nymph alongside Grad School Graduate and Darkness Blade. The three then later arrived at Shelter Nr. 7 after having failed in defeating the monster. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Red Muffler is one of many heroes who attempts to defeat Hundred-Eyes Octopus before Flashy Flash shows up. He appears to fight Hundred-Eyes Octopus but is nearly crushed before being saved by Bone. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Numbers. He and the other heroes try to stop Jumping Spider together but are easily blown away by the creature. As he is about to be eaten, Bang arrives and saves him. Pork Cutlet Bowl. Red Muffler was among the many heroes summoned by McCoy to combat the monster that was devastating the Z-City police station. He arrives at the scene late, after Saitama has already killed the monster. Abilities and Powers. Given his rank, it is safe to assume that he is fairly strong by C-Class standards. His power level is used as the control for Child Emperor's device and is set to 100. However, the fact that he has lost every fight he's been in, even with the assistance of B-Class and A-Class heroes implies that he is not very strong compared to other heroes. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Red Muffler has been shown to be quick on his feet, as seen when fighting Jumping Spider. Hero Rating. Red Muffler's rating determined by the Hero Association:

Red Nose Red Nose (, "Akahana"; Viz: Rednose) is the C-Class Rank 385 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. As his name suggests, Red Nose has a red nose. He also sports curly red hair, dull eyes, and a nonathletic build. He has apathetic eyes and constantly diagonal eyebrows. Red Nose is one of the shortest heroes, standing below most people whenever he is shown. He's also very portly, or fat. Personality. Red Nose is a rather selfish and attention-seeking individual, as seen when he kept looking at the camera and posing while trying to convince a man to refrain from committing suicide. He is also pretty cowardly given how he'd run from a monster at first sight and yet is highly overconfident, seeing Garou's rising infamy after defeating Tanktop Master as an opportunity for promotion and underestimating the Hero hunter due to the latter being a human. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Hero Hunt Arc. Red Nose begins to belittle the heroes that had been defeated by the Garou but gets negative responses from Hyottoko and Studless. He goes on to attempt to show off his own martial arts skills only to have Garou himself appear behind him. He and the heroes were later found beaten on the street. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Red Nose is later shown to have joined the Hero Name Victims Association, displeased with the name given to him by the Hero Association. He goes with the others to recruit Saitama at his apartment. He is present when the group protests outside the executive's meeting room as well. His "Desired Name" is Red Thunder. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Salmon. Red Nose is trying to convince a Suicidal Man not to jump from a building, but in reality, he is just trying to look good on camera. Numbers. Red Nose makes a cameo appearance when the Blizzard Group is talking about factions in the Hero Association. Abilities and Powers. Like most C-Class heroes, Red Nose seems to prefer to combine strength against emergencies, rather than fight them alone, as he was seen most of the time with other C-Class heroes. Given his rank in C-Class and how easily he was beaten by Garou, it can be assumed that Red Nose is a rather weak hero, even by C-Class standards. Fighting Style. Novice Martial Artist: When he spoke with Hyottoko and Studless about Garou, he claimed to know a bit about martial arts. Although he is clearly nowhere near Garou's level, who easily knocked him out. Equipment. Red Nose wears armor with a nose on the chest with the letter "R" on it, with additional noses on each of his shoulders, which extends through the arms to reach his gloves. The armor is made by his mother. Hero Rating. Red Nose's rating determined by the Hero Association:

Regeneration Regeneration is the ability to regrow certain body parts or cells that have been dismembered or destroyed and replace them with brand new cells, or simply regrouping all of their separated parts back together. Overview. There have been several beings capable of this, although each Mysterious Being has had different types of regeneration and different ways they have regenerated, and differed in how much time it takes to regenerate their bodies and whether they recreate cells in their body or regroup cells back together. Some humans and Mysterious Beings have a weaker version of this ability, and are able to regenerate fractured bones or mutilated body parts. Characters like Boros have an incredible rate of regeneration, with Boros himself surpassing all others of his race as stated by himself. He has been shown to regrow an arm in seconds just by concentrating his energy on it. When struck by Saitama's Consecutive Normal Punches, he was blown apart but was able to regenerate his whole body in an instant. However, Boros' regeneration ability has a limit, as it is shown in the end of the fight with Saitama, where he was unable to regenerate again after being struck by Saitama's Serious Punch due to him already having used up all his energy. Black Sperm possesses a unique regenerative ability; as his body is formed from vast numbers of copies of himself working together, any damage he sustains will reduce his total count, but his body is able to fully regenerate so long as he has reserves. Even if he is cut to pieces, his severed body parts will reform into more copies of himself. Orochi can regenerate his body from the brink of death by absorbing the blood of other creatures. However, it is only shown that he can regenerate from his heart.

Replication Replication is the ability to generate multiple copies of oneself. Overview. This ability enables the user to replicate themselves which they can use to do several different tasks at once or use their numbers to swarm and overwhelm their opponents in combat. Dr. Genus, through scientific means, can make a vast amount of clones of himself that he utilizes as assistants for his research. Melzargard is composed of five bodies, each with its own personality, which can freely separate to allow for attacks from multiple areas at once. Black Sperm can split into any number of clones that he chooses at will. Instead of dying, whenever he is dealt a fatal blow that would typically result in death, Black Sperm will automatically split into even more copies of himself as long as he has enough cell stock. This ability enables Black Sperm to easily overpower Atomic Samurai, an S-Class hero, with countless copies of himself during their battle.

Reptera Reptera (レプテラ, "Reputera") is a Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. She is the older sister of Raptora. Appearance. Reptera is a woman with a buxom humanoid shape and equipped with reptilian attributes: a tail, a body partially covered with scales, and sharp teeth. Her very long white puffy hair with two braids is decked out in dark feathers, as well as two straight black horns. Her outfit consists of pieces of camouflage fabric, black panties, spiked bracelets, and strappy heeled shoes. She is armed with daggers dripping with her venom. Personality. Reptera is hostile towards heroes. Puri Puri Prisoner left a terrifying impression on her both because of his power and his explanations that are beyond her. She has a bad temper as seen when she responds unrestrainedly to Baquma because he blamed his group for deviating from their mission for the Monster Association. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Reptera, alongside other Tiger-level monsters including Electric Catfish Man and Maiko Plasma, are attacking Puri-Puri Prisoner. When their attacks have no effect, they attempt to flee only to run into Baquma. Baquma tells them not to retreat, to which the monsters angrily ask him to fight the S-Class hero in their place. Baquma agrees and subsequently consumes them all to gain their powers. Shortly afterwards, she and the other monsters who were absorbed by Baquma are freed when Puri-Puri Prisoner defeats the elephant-like monster, with Reptera lying unconscious. Abilities & Powers. Supernatural Abilities. Poison Manipulation: As a poison-based Mysterious Being, Reptera has the ability to produce poison. Equipment. Knives: Reptera wields a pair of knives in combat.

Research Hybrid Monster An unnamed Mysterious Being that Tsukuyomi confined for experimental purposes. It went on a rampage years ago before being killed by Blast. Appearance. It was a relatively huge monster. It had claws, many sharp teeth and six eyes, somewhat resembling Overgrown Rover. It was also shown to be a quadruped, walking on all fours. It also has spiked, messy black hair on its head that goes down its back. History. This monster was assumed to be a cross breed between two monsters (as researchers referred to it as a "Hybrid Monster"). It escaped its containment, and went berserk attacking anyone who got in its way. It eventually came over to a young, 10-year-old Tatsumaki's holding cell as she was left to be abandoned. The monster smashed down the door, in an attempt to eat her. However, it was killed by Blast who managed to arrive in time to save Tatsumaki. Abilities and Powers. Its disaster level is unknown. It can be presumed that it was a fairly strong monster judging by its size and how dangerous it was to humans when it broke free. From the looks of it, it was easily killed by the top-ranking S-Class hero Blast. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: It appeared to be strong enough to break out of containment and be able to smash down a locked cell door.

Resurrection Resurrection is the ability for an individual to come back from a near-death experience. Overview. If the user is brought to the brink of death, the user is revived, rejuvenated, and becomes several times stronger. If the body is still intact, it appears the user can be resurrected any number of times. The potency of this ability is seen when Phoenix Man, through a single rebirth, was able to go from Disaster Level Demon to Disaster Level Dragon and additionally gained pyrokinesis. Before, he could not break a single invisible shield that Child Emperor had set up, but after his rebirth, he easily broke through all five of them at once. He also gained the ability to reanimate corpses to do his bidding, although they did not possess any of their original cognitive functions and only attacked blindly. The only one who has been shown to possess and utilize this ability is Phoenix Man. Phoenix Man attained this ability by being stuck in a costume of a TV show character that constantly dies and revives, so once he became a monster, he received those abilities.

Rhino Wrestler Rhino Wrestler (サイレスラー, "Sai Resurā") was a Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. He was killed by Atomic Samurai. Appearance. Rhino Wrestler was a humanoid biped creature with various body parts characteristic of a rhinoceros. He had the head of a rhino and was heavily built, with many layers of thick skin and armor on his body. He wore a wrestling singlet and had an armband on each arm. On his abdomen was a large tattoo. Personality. Rhino Wrestler was very prideful and eager to put his strength to the test. In addition, he desired to be praised by others. A testament to this can be seen when he asked Phoenix Man what he thought of Rhino Wrestler's disaster level. Like most other prideful monsters, he didn't care about compatibility with other heroes, with his only style of fighting being knocking down whoever comes in his way. Unlike most other monsters, Rhino Wrestler actually trained to hone his fighting abilities. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Rhino Wrestler, Phoenix Man, and Sludge Jellyfish stop Mohican and Pineapple when the two heroes were trying to leave the city with the soon-to-be hostages. Rhino Wrestler is left to the heroes by himself while the other monsters scout around. Rhino Wrestler is utterly bored by his opponents' pathetic attacks and decides to rate their attacks and scores all of them very lowly. After his rant about the heroes' strength, Rhino Wrestler boasts about his training towards his opponents and expresses his utter disappointment in the heroes that he is facing. Phoenix Man alerts Rhino Wrestler that it is time to leave and to take the hostages. In addition, he reminds Rhino Wrestler that today is not the "main event", so they can't do as they please. Finally, Rhino Wrestler is told to only take the son of the Hero Association sponsor. Mohican and Pineapple make a final desperate attempt to stop Rhino Wrestler, but fail miserably as Rhino Wrestler is able to easily charge through them. Afterwards, Elder Centipede grabs Phoenix Man and Rhino Wrestler and leaves in the hole he created earlier. Monster Association Arc. In the Monster Association, Maiko Plasma, Electric Catfish Man, and a few other monsters are discussing amongst themselves, while Rhino Wrestler is training. The other monsters are impressed by the victory Maiko Plasma and Electric Catfish Man had over Lightning Genji. The pair of monsters states that Gyoro Gyoro was the one who ordered them to fight Lightning Genji, and that as long as the monsters fight who Gyoro Gyoro tells them to fight, they won't lose. Rhino Wrestler interjects and states compatibility as "stupid". He boasts that he will knock down whoever comes in his own way, and completely destroys the punching bag he was using to train, reveling in the knowledge he will soon prove his strength. Prior to the monster raid, Rhino Wrestler goes to Gyoro Gyoro and asks him if he was still Tiger level. Gyoro Gyoro replies by saying when he first met him, he was, but after his training, he had progressed to be a Demon level threat. He said he wanted to see Rhino Wrestler fight as soon as possible. Gyoro Gyoro then continues by saying among the many monsters, there were a few monsters who achieved significant growth in a short period of time, and he was pleased when this occurred. He was one of the second wave of monsters who attacked the heroes. Needle Star is the first to attack, striking Rhino Wrestler with Violence Star attack, but the monster easily knocks him back, rating his attack as a 25 out of 100. Next, Mizuki jumps into the air and attacks him with her Shot Put, but he brushes the attack off, giving her 30 points and prepares to attack her, but Needle Star grabs her hand and pulls her out of way. She thanks Needle Star, and he warns the heroes of his enhanced power. The next one to attack is One Shotter, who fires many rounds in an attempt to break his horn, but Rhino Wrestler is able to see and deflect all of his shots and rates his attack as a 15, leaving him shocked. Rhino Wrestler charges the heroes, with thoughts of his desires to be the strongest running inside his head. Jet Nice Guy attacks his left cheek, but it fails to damage him and he gives the hero 10 points. Then, Shadow Ring strikes the monster with her sword, yet it does very little, as he rates it as only 10 points. Rhino Wrestler yells out for all the heroes to attack him so he can give them all scores, so the next one to fight him is Iaian. The A-class hero unsheathes his sword and strikes his horn, momentarily halting the monster's movement. Rhino Wrestler rates his attack 69 points, and the others see it as the opportune moment to strike together. First, Jet Nice Guy attacks with his Ultimate Jet Straight across the monster's face; next, Double Fall tickles his nose to activate his energy sneeze. Crescent Eyebroll uses his Crescent Consecutive Slashes, while Narcissistoic uses his Rose American Sack attack, and the rest of the heroes join in, but Rhino Wrestler is able to blow all of them away, rating each of their attacks. The heroes are shocked at his power, while Rhino Wrestler reminisces of a moment when Gyoro Gyoro conversed with Rhino Wrestler before the monster raid and how Gyoro Gyoro commended the monster for the increase in strength, and Rhino Wrestler screams out for the strongest heroes to fight him, all-the-while fighting Iaian. Rhino Wrestler is able to hold Iaian back, but before the battle can continue further, Atomic Samurai tells his disciple he would take his place. Iaian insists he can handle it, but Atomic Samurai tells him he will cut off his horn himself. Rhino Wrestler derides Atomic Samurai for fighting him singlehandedly after witnessing him effortlessly handle the other heroes, but he then commends him for his spirit. Rhino Wrestler yells for Atomic Samurai to use his killer move to score, and he throws a punch at Atomic Samurai. Less than a second later, Atomic Samurai tells the others they were done there and it was time to advance, and he begins to walk past the monster. Rhino Wrestler insists the battle isn't over, and demands Atomic Samurai not ignore him. Suddenly, Atomic Samurai remembers what the monster said before and asks Rhino Wrestler for his score. Rhino Wrestler's eyes widen, and as his horn falls off, he clutches the stub that was once his horn and begins to tremble. He laments that Gyoro Gyoro lied to him, as he stated Rhino Wrestler was "strong enough to defeat the S-class". His final words are rating Atomic Samurai's score a 100 out of 100, before he is sliced into hundreds of tiny pieces. Atomic Samurai thanks Rhino Wrestler for his perfect score before moving on to kill the other monsters. Abilities and Powers. Rhino Wrestler was a very powerful monster, capable of overpowering multiple A, B, and C-Class heroes simultaneously with ease, and was able to fight on par with Iaian, the 2nd highest ranked A-Class hero who has the potential to reach S-Class. However, he was completely defenseless against Atomic Samurai, and was sliced by the hero's Atomic Slash before he even realized what was happening. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: Rhino Wrestler possessed enormous strength, strong enough to easily knock out Mohican and Pineapple simultaneously in a single attack, as well as knock back multiple A, B, and C-Class heroes. Additionally, he was capable of breaking apart a series of very large tires chained together into a punching bag with apparent ease. When fighting Iaian, an A-Class hero with potential for S-Class, Rhino Wrestler was strong enough to stop a powerful blow from the hero. Immense Durability: Rhino Wrestler possessed amazing toughness, capable of withstanding numerous attacks from C, B and even A-Class heroes without any damage. Additionally, his horn was durable enough to take the sword strikes of Iaian and remain practically unscathed, despite Iaian being capable of cutting through Tongara's highly durable battle suit. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: Rhino Wrestler was able to perform a series of fast punches while training on a punching bag, and later overwhelmed a large group of heroes with his rapid attacks. He was fast enough to react to the bullets from One Shotter, who used a sniper rifle to attack him, very quickly and deflect each shot with his horn. Enhanced Growth Rate: Rhino Wrestler has shown capable of rapidly growing stronger through training. By training hard day after day, he managed to vastly increase his strength and even raise his disaster level from Tiger to Demon. Furthermore, as stated by himself, Rhino Wrestler can get stronger in the midst of a fight. Fighting Style. Proficient Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Rhino Wrestler preferred close-quarters combat and believed the only effective method is to knock down any opponent that comes his way. He commonly used his horn as both a defensive tool and an offensive weapon. He was skilled enough to accurately judge the techniques of others, and rated techniques of B-Class and C-Class heroes very poorly.

Tech Tech (テック, "Tekku") is a Machine God (機神, "Kishin") battle robot created by The Organization. It was destroyed by Genos. Appearance. Tech is a fairly tall robot with a knight-like design. Its head possessed a single eye and four claw-like extensions from the sides. It wielded a fearsome longsword and had a furry cape flowing from its shoulders. Personality. Tech presents itself as arrogant and self-righteous. In addition, Tech is quite condescending, mocking Genos' anger towards the death of Dr. Kuseno and calling it a pointless sentiment. Despite this, it is capable of recognizing the strength of its opponents, noting that with Genos' unique abilities, he could've risen to the top of the hero world if he had more time to hone his powers. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Tech joins Body, Ray, and several other robots in attacking Dr. Kuseno's laboratory, killing the doctor. It then engages in battle with Genos, taunting him over the death of his mentor before being destroyed. Abilities and Powers. As a Dragon-level threat of the Organization, Tech is a very powerful Mysterious Being. Alongside its partners, Tech was capable of pressuring Genos even with his new upgrades, forcing the cyborg to use his last resort to keep up. Robotic Abilities. Immense Strength: Tech possesses incredible strength, capable of holding its own against Genos with ease. Immense Durability: Tech is remarkably durable. It was capable of taking Genos' High Voltage Tackle without serious damage. However, a powerful Super Incineration Cannon from Genos managed to shatter it. Immense Speed and Reflexes: Tech is very fast, capable of keeping up with Genos in combat. Even after Genos unleashed his Roaring Dragon Core, Tech was still able to momentarily keep up with the cyborg's speed before being overwhelmed. Fighting Style. Swordsmanship: Tech carries a big sword to engage in close-quarters combat. Equipment. Sword: Tech uses a big sword to engage in combat. This weapon was durable enough to withstand a few of Genos's punches before being snapped in half by an uppercut from the cyborg.

Technique Mimicry Technique Mimicry is the ability to copy techniques and/or skills of another. Overview. Users of this ability can replicate the techniques and/or skills of those whom they've fought against or witnessed in the heat of battle; this can have varying degrees of success, with some individuals being able to mimic them perfectly whilst others can only produce lackluster copies. The results of mimicking a skill can depend on a number of different factors, such as the potential of the copier or whether the original user performed said technique at its highest level. Usage. Garou. Garou is capable of memorizing an opponents movements thereby allowing him to copy their fighting style after only seeing it once, such as when he replicated Watchdog Man's moves to an unknown extent and utilized them against Genos during their battle or when he managed to use Bomb's Whirlwind Iron Cutting Fist against Royal Ripper after only seeing it once; albeit he could only perform a lesser variation of it at first. Nevertheless, being a prodigy in martial arts as well as overcoming a near suicidal degree of training by thrashing entire dojos and hunting down heroes, Garou improved Bomb's fighting style to a level where he could use the Cross Fang Dragon Slayer Fist alone when it normally requires two fighters working in tandem in order to function. After being mutated by "God" and achieving his Cosmic Fear Mode, Garou's ability to replicate fighting styles has been enhanced to where he's capable of even duplicating the S-Class Rank 1 hero, Blast's abilities to create portals and manipulate gravity during their short exchange. Orochi. Orochi, who's a combat prodigy in a similar vein as that of Garou, has demonstrated himself to be capable of perfectly copying Garou's Water Stream Rock Smashing Fist after only briefly glancing it once during their fight. He can utilize this martial arts just as well as the Hero Hunter. G5. G5 has also shown itself to have copied Atomic Samurai's signature technique, Atomic Slash. However, his version of the attack was of a much lesser extent compared to that of the S-Class hero's and, as a result, G5 lost his battle against the swordsmen. Saitama. In his against Awakened Garou: Cosmic Fear Mode, it's revealed that Saitama possesses the ability to learn and master any techniques or powers of his opponents just by witnessing them once, being similar to but even better than Garou himself. This means that should Saitama so wish, he can grasp and master any martial arts instantly, despite him being unironically regarded as an "amateur" by others on several occasions. He has shown the capability to copy not only Garou's extremely advanced martial arts but also his more supernatural abilities such as time travel.

Telepathy Telepathy (テレパシー, Terepashī) is the ability to know what is in someone else's mind, or to communicate with them, without using words or any other kind of physical signal. Overview. The user is able to read thoughts and speak with others mentally. This ability is primarily used by Espers. Telepathy is first used in the series when Slugerous attempts to communicate with Kamakyuri which allowed him to learn the latter was killed by Saitama without having to be present. During Melzargard's battle against the other S-Class heroes, Geryuganshoop is shown using telepathy to mentally communicate with him, telling him to return to the Giant Spaceship. After Garou awakens from his unconscious state after his battle with the heroes, Gyoro Gyoro uses telepathy to communicate with the Hero Hunter, telling him to stay hidden while he deals with the other members of the Monster Association. During his battle against Child Emperor, Phoenix Man demonstrated himself to have minor telepathic capabilities, allowing him to mentally communicate with the hero. More remarkably, Phoenix Man is even able to connect his and Child Emperor's within a spiritual space, a place separate from the real world where he and the child hero can talk in peace, even though their physical body isn't there. While being restrained by Tatsumaki's unrivaled psychic powers, Psykos attempts to communicate with Overgrown Rover using telepathy, asking for the executive's assistance. 18 years ago, after saving Tatsumaki from a hybrid monster, when Blast placed his hand on her head, he saw a vision of Fubuki and could tell that she's her sister. Due to this, it is implied that he may have some sort of psychic or mind-reading ability. Later, when Tatsumaki falls unconscious due to exhaustion from the battle against Psykos and Orochi, Fubuki uses telepathy to psychically contact her.

Tentacle Muffler Tentacle Muffler (触手マフラー, "Shokushu Mafurā") was a Mysterious Being. It was killed by the "Puri-Puri Prison Partners". Appearance. Tentacle Muffler resembles a man with hairy legs dressed in shorts with a number of mufflers wrapped together around her head, concealing his features except for his eyes which are just barely visible through a gap in his mufflers. Personality. Nothing is known about Tentacle Muffler's personality. Abilities and Powers. As a Wolf-level Myster Being, Tentacle Muffler was quite weak and was defeated by a group of prisoners working under Puri-Puri Prisoner.

Terror Lizard Clan The Terror Lizard Clan (恐竜族, Kyōryū-zoku) was a clan of dinosaurs that used to live on Earth eons ago. They were wiped out when a meteor crashed into the Earth. The Ancient King, the sole survivor of the clan, later tried to take over the surface of the Earth by himself but was killed by Tatsumaki. Overview. The Terror Lizard Clan was a violent race who used to roam the Earth. They were colossal creatures that had various reptilian animal features, such as scales and claws. The King had the ability to shoot Energy Beams from his mouth. Plot. Hero Association Saga. Alien Conquerors Arc. The Ancient King awakens after 300,000,000 years of slumber, which he spent waiting for the kings of the other clans to be taken out. He is attacked by Earth's military forces, but the missiles prove ineffective against the Terror Lizard's skin. The Hero Association deploys Tatsumaki who takes care of the Mysterious Being.

The Blizzard Group Arc The Blizzard Group Arc is the eleventh arc of the "One-Punch Man" series and the second arc of the Human Monster Saga. Plot. Three Figures enter the isolated area in Z-City. They are revealed to be the three top three ranked B-Class heroes Fubuki, Eyelashes and Mountain Ape respectively, who are moving toward their "target." Meanwhile, at Saitama's house, Genos reveals that the two have been promoted to B-Class Rank 7 (Saitama) and S-Class Rank 14 (Genos), and although Saitama neglected to report his work, it was still reported by eyewitnesses, which causes Genos to believe his master is finally being recognized. Genos senses an object coming in at an abnormal speed and rushes outside, trying not to disturb Saitama. The object is revealed to be Speed-o'-Sound Sonic who recognizes Genos from their previous meeting. Sonic then claims he came to battle Saitama as his rival, which angers Genos, causing both to prompt each other into a fight. At the same time, Saitama overwrites a save data on King's handheld gaming console which he took from King's apartment. 20 minutes later, the three B-Class heroes are outside Saitama's door, with Eyelashes yelling at him to come out. Blizzard of Hell introduces herself to Saitama, but Saitama is not impressed. She then tells him off of the factions in the Hero Association and threatens him to work under her. Saitama refuses, which causes both Eyelashes and Mountain Ape to attack him, but the two are then swiftly defeated. After Saitama defeated her subordinates, Fubuki uses her psychic powers, but Saitama is not surprised by her abilities. She uses a technique called Hell Storm, which leaves her opponent's bone cracked and flesh ripped apart, but Saitama managed to get behind her and patronized her on being a hero. Fubuki was angered by his statement and use a barrage of different techniques, all of which were ineffective against Saitama. She tearfully attacks Saitama with a box cutter but was caught up in Genos' and Sonic's attack. She managed to evade the attack, only because Saitama came in between the explosion. She meets Genos and was surprised at the fact he was Saitama's disciple. Sonic threw an Exploding Shuriken at Genos, but the attack was ineffective. Sonic comes down from atop the street light, boasting that he shall beat Genos and Saitama shall be next. Meanwhile, Fubuki notices his killing intent and claims him to be dangerous. Genos tells Saitama that he shall beat Sonic, to which Sonic is amused as he claims Genos to be slow. Genos then responds that he did not show what he is truly capable of. Genos then accelerates himself and quickly moves behind Sonic, unsuccessfully attacking yet again because Sonic manages to catch on and dodge. Saitama and Fubuki witness the match and while Saitama notices Genos moving faster than he did when they fought, even hypothesizing that he got new parts, Fubuki is unable to keep up with the speed of the two. After a bit of fighting, Sonic notices Genos keeps getting behind him, thinking he is mocking his speed. Genos then drops Sonic's topknot, leaving him with short hair, which angers Sonic. Genos gets behind Sonic and attacks with his Machine Gun Blow technique, only to be surprised to learn he had only hit an afterimage. Sonic then retaliates with his secret technique: Four Shadows Burial - Scattered Flash Slash, which Genos cannot follow. This prompts Genos to blow up the entire area, going at maximum power. Afterward, as Sonic is thought to have beaten Genos, he realizes Genos had fallen before he was able to cut him. Learning Saitama was responsible, he calls him soft for wanting to protect his pupil, to which Saitama replies it was to prevent Genos from destroying the place since they live in the vicinity. Saitama then tells Genos to stop his fight as he himself was Sonic's target, then states he shall take Sonic on seriously. Sonic then states he shall use the ultimate technique he developed, in order to kill Saitama. Meanwhile, Fubuki is watching the entire fight and is glad she's ignored for otherwise, she might have been in danger. Sonic attacks Saitama with his ultimate technique: Ten Shadows Burial, to which both Genos and Fubuki are impressed but are still capable of seeing. He does not have the upper hand and Saitama counters with his own super move: Serious Series - Serious Side Hops, creating an infinite amount of clones and beating Sonic. Sonic then appears to be knocked out, which to Genos resembles death, but Sonic managed to instantly leave. Fubuki, seeing everything, claims Saitama to be too strong. Fubuki explains the reason why she stays in B-Class is that she will never reach the top of the ranks like her sister Tatsumaki. As such, when she became B-Class she took control of the lower heroes in order to surpass her sister, who is a lone wolf. Genos comments she could be at the top of A-Class, but Fubuki states that it is impossible, because she will never be Rank 1. She explains that Atomic Samurai's three disciples Bushidrill, Okamaitachi, and Iaian are unable to get to S-Class, because of Sweet Mask, who is securing Rank 1. Meanwhile, Suppon, a caveman who escaped from a nearby lab, is causing havoc on the streets, and Sweet Mask was ordered to bring it back alive. The caveman hisses at him, but Sweet Mask comments he isn't that sweet. Suppon attacks Sweet Mask, but he easily dodges and counter attacks the caveman, killing him instantly, with the crowd cheering for him. At Saitama's apartment, Fubuki tells Saitama that he might be a monster himself, but nowhere near Sweet Mask or Tatsumaki. Fubuki tries to justify her action, though Saitama has nothing against it; he doesn't feel like being her henchman. Moments later, much to Fubuki's shock and awe, King arrives, asking for his game. Saitama returns the game, admitting he accidentally erased King's data. Fubuki, surprised at how S-Class heroes are attracted by Saitama's strength, begins thinking about joining the others. At the Hero Association meeting, Saitama and Genos are given hero names. Genos is named Demon Cyborg, while Saitama is simply named Caped Baldy. Sitch is furious over the meeting, debating names rather than about Garou's rampage. They explained Bang volunteered to get rid of Garou and there is King, Tatsumaki, and Blast if all else fails. Meanwhile, Garou coincidentally, ran into Tanktop Vegetarian, and defeats him, but was not satisfied by the fight. He happily announces his hero hunt and couldn't wait to fight S-class heroes.

The Brain and Brawn Brothers The Brain and Brawn Brothers (天才と筋肉兄弟, "Tensai to Kinniku Kyōdai") was a self-proclaimed team of the genius older brother, Fukegao, and the muscular younger brother, Marugori. When Fukegao invented the steroid, Biceps Brachii King, his brother ingested it and transformed into a mutated giant. Together, they allegedly combined the highest intelligence and highest physical power and strove to control the world. The brothers destroyed D-City, and soon after, Saitama was found on Marugori's shoulder. Fukegao told Marugori to kill him and he accidentally killed Fukegao. Saitama then defeated Marugori, wrecking B-City in the process.

The Extended Family of Darkness The Extended Family of Darkness (闇の大家族, "Yami no Dai Kazoku") is a group of Mysterious Beings. Appearance. The Extended Family of Darkness is a group of at least eleven dark humanoid monsters of varying sizes and body types. They all have a devilish appearance including varying sets of eyes, sharp teeth and claws, forked tails, and they also each have two sets of wings with varying appearances, one being on their back and one being on their head. Personality. Not much is known about their personalities. Since they act as a group and their name mentions them being a "family", it can be inferred that they have a strong familial bond and care about one another. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. The Extended Family of Darkness suddenly appear in T-City and the Hero Association quickly designates them as disaster level Dragon. Later on, Genos arrives at the scene and they prepare to face him. After exchanging blows with the group of monsters, Genos finishes the battle with an explosive blast from his core. The Extended Family of Darkness was defeated, although the battle severely damaged the cyborg. The majority of T-City is destroyed in the battle. In the original webcomic, this was the first Dragon-level threat Genos was able to suppress on his own. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about The Extended Family of Darkness. Given that they are a Dragon-level threat, it can be assumed that they are an extremely strong group of monsters. It can be assumed that they use their numbers to their advantage. Despite being defeated by Genos, they managed to destroy his right arm and leave him in critical condition at the end of the battle.

The Great Degenerate The Great Degenerate (どすけべ, "Dosukebe") is the B-Class Rank 100 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. The Great Degenerate is a man with dark hair and two scars over each of his eyes. He wears a face mask over his mouth and nose, and a set of body armor around his torso. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. The Great Degenerate is part of the Hero Name Victims Association, and goes with them to request Saitama to join them. He is later seen protesting with the rest of the group outside the Hero Association's executive meeting room, demanding to know why he was called the Great Degenerate in the first place. His "Desired Name" is Magic Hand. Powers & Abilities. Cybernetic Hands: The Great Degenerate's hands are mechanical, and he can fire them and control them remotely.

The Great Food Tub The Great Food Tub (ダイショッカン, "Daishokkan"; Viz: Big Eater) was a Demon-Level Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. He was killed by Pig God. Appearance. In the webcomic, The Great Food Tub resembled a pig with a human body. He had two very sharp bottom teeth, pointed ears and the nostrils of a pig. In the manga, his appearance drastically changed, having the appearance of a very large . Personality. The Great Food Tub had a very gluttonous personality, and he desired to consume all the heroes. Although he preferred eating humans, he had no problem eating a fellow monster when presented to him. After G5 fed him a monster, The Great Food Tub left and apologized for blocking the way. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. The Great Food Tub is first seen encountering Royal Ripper as he escorts Tareo to his cell and tries to eat Tareo. However, Royal Ripper states that the child is his and sarcastically asks The Great Food Tub to cut his own tail to satisfy his own hunger. Subsequently, The Great Food Tub tries to attack G5 as the latter tries to pass through, but G5 grabs a monster and throws it at The Great Food Tub's mouth, causing him to eat the monster on the spot. The Great Food Tub then leaves the scene satisfied. The Great Food Tub eventually comes across Pig God, giving a monologue about his status as the gluttonous monster that will consume all heroes whole before lunging at the hero. Atomic Samurai's disciples later witness him being swallowed alive by Pig God. Original Webcomic. Great Food Tub is first seen in the Webcomic with the other monsters, preparing for the attack against the heroes invading their headquarters. Great Food Tub notices Royal Ripper's absence and asks Black Sperm where he is, to which Black Sperm replies he is most likely torturing Tareo. He is later killed in a similar manner as in the manga. Abilities and Powers. Based on his status as a Demon-level threat, he was likely very strong. He ate his opponents. However, very little can be said beyond that, as he is consumed by Pig God before he could show off any of his abilities, leaving the exact details of his power unknown.

The Mediocre Ability Users The Mediocre Ability Users are a trio of criminals who inexplicably have obtained supernatural abilities. However, as their title would imply, they aren't very powerful. Appearances in Other Media. OVAs. Saitama and the Mediocre Ability Users. The group meets up in-person for the first time in a public restroom, having previously met online. They discuss their plans to pull off a crime, though they note that they spoke with a fourth guy who should be there but never showed up. They soon run into Saitama and mistake him for their ally. However, when he introduces himself as a hero, they attack him. Their attacks misfire completely and they end up getting saved from themselves by Saitama, and start contemplating about how weak their abilities are compared to the likes of Tatsumaki, Fubuki, and Volten, who use their respective abilities to earn a living. They have a change of heart and decide to work together to make it big. However, the group is then attacked by Dirt Earthworm, who tries to crush them with a wall of earth. They are saved by Saitama again, who sends the monster flying. Genos arrives at the scene after following the evacuation warning, only to find Saitama there alone with The Mediocre Ability Users, who he thinks are troubling his master. They quickly lie about how they just aspire to be heroes and wanted to spar with Saitama. Genos tries to get them to leave, but Saitama believes them and decides to train them. He forces them to do his special workout, at which point they're too scared to stop and tell him the truth.

The Mysterious Shrine A mysterious ancient shrine located deep underground in Z-City. It was found by Orochi. According to him, even Psykos isn't aware of this place. Description. The area near this shrine is flooded with . There are several stone pillars and a staircase which leads to a tablet. On this tablet, there is a depiction of a monster bearing a similar appearance to Orochi being given sacrifices by several humans. There is also an ancient text foretelling the resurrection of a god after a worthy sacrifice is given. However, hidden behind the stone is an image of a larger being and the actual "God" the text spoke of. Background. Orochi found the shrine after he began venturing further into deep underground in an attempt to grow stronger by draining energy directly from the deepest parts of the Earth. When Orochi approached the shrine, he discovered a tablet which depicted him and stated that a worthy sacrifice was needed in order to resurrect "God", leading him to believe that it was referring to him as a god. From that point onwards, the Monster King always searched for a "worthy sacrifice" that was required for his resurrection as a god according to the tablet until he met Saitama. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. During his encounter with Saitama in the Monster Association Headquarters, Orochi believes that the Caped Baldy is a worthy sacrifice for his resurrection as a god before leading him to deep underground where the shrine is located. After being defeated by Saitama who lands a single punch on him that blows his body apart, Orochi's remnants crawl to the shrine as the place begins collapsing. When he is right in front of the tablet, a full image of the actual "God" appears in the mural's prophecy and is unseen by him. When Tatsumaki finishes off Orochi with her large spear, the shrine is seen again as Orochi's body is torn apart.

The Ominous Future The Ominous Future (な, "Fukitsuna Mirai") is the disastrous future that happens during the fight between Saitama and Garou. After defeating Garou, Saitama changes this future by reversing time. Event. Having transformed under the influence of "God" and achieved his Cosmic Fear Mode that results in incredible power, Garou battles Saitama once again. After hitting Saitama with his Gamma Ray Burst and sending him flying away, Garou confronts many heroes on the surface of the ruined Z-City in the absence of Saitama. Due to being influenced by "God", Garou's body automatically emits radiation potent enough to cause the heroes present to pass out and even threaten all life on Earth. Seeing such a massive threat, Blast, the S-Class Rank 1 hero, shows up and attempts to stop the Hero Hunter. After a brief scuffle between the two, Garou decides that Blast isn't worthy of his time and switches his attention to Genos and impales the cyborg through his chest before tearing off his power core, killing him. Later, Saitama returns and is depressed to discover that his disciple and many other heroes have been killed by Garou, while Blast, who is still fine, watches and warns the Caped Baldy to stay back. However, now enraged and overcome with grief, Saitama charges at Garou with a Serious Punch, which the Hero Hunter copies and attempts to counter-act with his own Serious Punch. Sensing the immense power behind their fists, Blast immediately teleports them to space out of fear that the planet will be destroyed. Now outside of Earth's atmosphere, Saitama and Garou collide their fists which emits massive waves of energy that threaten to destroy the Earth beneath. Seeing as Blast is unable to handle the energy on his own, three of his comrades show up and offer him help and together, they manage to redirect the energy released from the two fighter's punches away from the planet. Saitama and Garou are subsequently launched to Io, a moon of Jupiter, by the recoil of their own punches. The two of them resume their battle, with Saitama ultimately coming out victorious and Garou regretting his actions that led to Tareo's death, who, along with many other heroes, also succumbed to the radiation emitted from Garou. Repentant of this, Garou decides to pass on to Saitama his most powerful technique that involves the manipulation of time in hope that the hero can master it to travel backwards in time. Moments after executing his technique, Garou is killed by "God" but not before Saitama manages to get hold of the technique and successfully begins to travel through time.
