Saitama goes back to the past, bringing with him the core of the deceased Genos from the future, and arrives at the moment when Garou, right after releasing his Gamma Ray Burst, appeared in front of many heroes. With a single punch to the face, he utterly defeats Garou this time without letting the Ominous Future happen again. Now having successfully changed the future, Saitama is forcibly thrown back into his "past" self and becomes one with him, unable to remember what happened in the Ominous Future. Suffered defeat from a mysterious knockout punch, a confused Garou screams in pain as God's powers begin to leave his body, while the heroes present are shocked to watch him. Aftermath. After returning to the past and becoming one with his "past" self, Saitama is now unable to remember what's happened but the core of the deceased Genos from the Ominous Future is still in his hand. Saitama is shocked to see the depleted core and worried about the disciple while the now-alive Genos rushes towards him. Seeing that the core in Saitama's hand resembles his own core, Genos tries making it function by plugging a sub-connector into it. Instantly after doing so, the memories contained in the core that had crossed time and space with Saitama flow into the cyborg and momentarily stun him. Genos soon asserts that the core is indeed his and wonders if those memories from it are from a future that could have happened. He then tries to retell everything that happened in the Ominous Future to Saitama in a very lengthy way, which confuses Saitama who doesn't want to listen and simply tells him to stop. Believing that Saitama is pretending not to remember and that he is the only one who knows about the fact that Saitama had crossed time and space to save everyone, Genos smiles and tells Saitama that he is a true hero, while thinking that he must let others who need to know be aware of this as well.

The Organization The Organization (, "Soshiki") is a secret group composed of various robots. Their goal is to cause destruction and chaos as well as fight powerful opponents in order to collect more combat data so as to increase their own power. Plot. Introduction Saga. Paradise Group Arc. The Organization allow Hammerhead and the Paradisers to steal battle suits produced by them in order to collect battle data. Once Hammerhead was defeated and the suits were destroyed, two members of the Organization were sent in order to finish him off and leave after believing him to be dead. However, Hammerhead manages to survive due to his thick skull. Hero Association Saga. King Arc. The Organization sends Machine God, G4 to fight S-Class Rank 7 hero, King and collect his data. However, King runs away, leaving Genos to fight the robot. After defeating G4, Genos sends its parts to Dr. Kuseno to be used for upgrades for his cyborg body. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Narinki takes armor developed by the Organization and gives them to a squad in order to save his son, Waganma. However, the Organization is actually in cahoots with the Monster Association as they send their latest fighting robot, G5 to assist the Monster Association. After making his way to the Monster Association HQ, G5 manages to capture Narinki's mercenaries and hand them over to the Monster Association to be turned into foot soldiers by Do-S. G5 is holding the head of a Metal Knight Unit and calls it a valuable sample. G5 confronts Child Emperor during his attempt to rescue Waganma, but Child Emperor and Waganma manage to escape. The robot later encounters Atomic Samurai, and is defeated in the ensuing battle. However, his core escapes before it could be destroyed. G5 later appears on the surface of the Monster Association HQ in the Z-City Ghost Town, interrupting Sekingar and Drive Knight's conversation and shooting off the former's arm. Before he could kill Sekingar, however, Genos appears and destroys G5 with a swift stomp. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. In the chaos brought on by the sudden appearance of many monsters, Machine God Mirror is sent to retrieve data on King. It is met by Suiko. After managing to defeat multiple heroes and Suiko, the robot is then destroyed by Saitama. Later, multiple robots including several Machine Gods such as Body, Ray, and Tech are sent to Kuseno's Laboratory to eliminate Dr. Kuseno and Genos. They succeed in fatally wounding Kuseno. However; Genos manages to defeat the three Machine God battle robots after a tough battle against them. Having only 9% of his energy left, the cyborg hero successfully destroys two more of them while the remaining robots are wrecked by Saitama. As a result of their raid, Kuseno and his lab are gone. Three Machine God robots such as Magnesauza, Slice, and Eguro also show up and target strong individuals such as Garou, Puri-Puri Prisoner, and Zombieman respectively. They want to take the bodies of the latter three for the modification of soldiers. However, only Eguro succeeds in capturing Zombieman while the other two are destroyed by their targets.

The Rampaging Cyborg The Rampaging Cyborg (暴走サイボーグ, "Bōsō Saibōgu") is the cyborg that destroyed the home town of Genos and murdered his family. Since then it is his archenemy. Appearance. The Rampaging Cyborg has a brief appearance during a conversation between Drive Knight and Genos. It appears to look like a humanoid robot. Personality. The Rampaging Cyborg is insane and uncontrolled, having destroyed everything in sight at Genos's town. According to Genos, this is probably because a failed body modification generated an irregularity in its brain. History. Four years before Genos met Saitama, the Rampaging Cyborg attacked the former's hometown, destroying everything and even murdering his family with Genos being the only known survivor. While tracking down the Rampaging Cyborg, Dr. Kuseno came to the ruined town and found Genos. It's also been known as the Mad Cyborg. Drive Knight claims that the rampaging cyborg destroyed his village too, and that he thus has a similar past to Genos. He did not give a specific time frame. Drive Knight tells Genos that the Rampaging Cyborg is a creation made by Bofoi. It is also revealed by Dr. Kuseno that the Rampaging Cyborg too killed the scientist's family in one of the villages it went around destroying. Plot. House of Evolution Arc. After meeting Saitama, Genos first mentions the Rampaging Cyborg to him. Genos soon encounters Armored Gorilla and suspects him to be the Rampaging Cyborg but it turns out he is not the one Genos is looking for. Genos then questions Armored Gorilla about any other cyborgs within the House of Evolution. Neo Heroes Introduction Arc. No hero records have been shown to take down the Rampaging Cyborg and it has not shown up for a few years. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc It is theorised that it is most likely in sleep mode, hidden away with the rest of Bofoi's robotic creations. Abilities and Powers. Although the full extent of what the Rampaging Cyborg is capable of is unknown, based on what Genos has mentioned, it can be inferred that this rampaging cyborg is very powerful and dangerous. It was able to completely ruin Genos's town, having destroyed everything there including parks, schools, and buildings.

The Strong Among the Ordinary The Strong Among the Ordinary (強一般人, "Kyō Ippanjin") is an extra chapter included with Volume 24. Summary. A monster named Dark introduces himself. He wishes to be the strongest monster in history and wants to make a name for himself by assassinating an S-Class hero as his start. Dark arrives at a venue where an S-Class hero is having a fan meetup, and plans on disguising himself as one of the fans and striking down the S-Class hero by surprise. Upon arriving, he is asked to get in line among the fans in order to meet the hero. As he opposes, a fan approaches and grabs his arm, with him being unable to break free. Dark is amazed by the fan's strength, who he suspects to be a hero slipped in as a normal human. Another one then comes and easily restrains him, much to his shock. As they are revealed to be Superalloy Darkshine's ardent fans, all of them surround Dark and begin stripping his and their own clothes, exposing their extreme muscular bodies, even more muscular than he himself. After the meeting with Darkshine and seeing the demonstration of the hero's strength, Dark is discouraged and flees as Saitama runs into him and asks him if he is fine.
The Style of a King The Style of a King (の, "Kingu no Fūkaku") is an extra chapter included with Volume 30.

The Three Crows The Three Crows (ガラス, "Sanbagarasu") were a group of Mysterious Beings and members of the Monster Association. They were each killed by Lightning Max, Sneck, and Suiryu. Appearance. The Three Crows had the typical appearance of a black crow. They were very large and had three legs and muscular human arms. History. The Three Crows used to be Gouketsu's disciples. They were weak-willed and lost their personas after monsterification. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Super Fight Arc. After the Super Fight had ended, The Three Crows fly inside the C-City Super Stadium and hold Rosie, Dave and Bazuzu hostage. They then attack and defeat the martial artists, enforcing Gouketsu's offer on them and not letting them escape. However, they are killed by the combined force of Suiryu, Sneck, and Max. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about The Three Crows. Given the fact they were a Demon-level threat, it is presumed that they were fairly strong. They were strong enough to easily defeat several martial artists. Each individual crow was presumably around a Tiger-level threat since A-Class heroes like Lightning Max and Sneck were able to challenge and defeat them. Physical Abilities. Flight: Their feathered wings allowed the Crows to fly. Enhanced Strength: They were able to wound Suiryu with their punches, although this was when he was already significantly weakened and had a broken arm. Enhanced Durability: One of the crows survived a Lightning Kick from Lightning Max. Fighting Style. Expert Hand-to-Hand Combatant: As disciples under Gouketsu from when they were human, they were trained in martial arts. While they lost their egos, they retained their combat skills and could use their beaks, fists, and claws to attack opponents. They had good teamwork. Trivia. The Three Crows are a reference to a number of mythological creatures:

The Three Tempest Brothers The Three Tempest Brothers (テンペスト三兄弟, "Tenpesuto San Kyōdai") were a group of Mysterious Beings and members of the Monster Association. Appearance. One of the brothers looked like a bug, one had horns, pointed ears, and six eyes, and one looked like a squid. Plot. Omake. Reality Punch. The brothers attempt to defeat Saitama, but the hero easily kills the six-eyed one with a single punch. The other two run away. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about their abilities.

Three-Eyed Ghost Three-Eyed Ghost (三つゴースト, "Mittsume Gōsuto") was a Tiger-level Mysterious Being. It was an aggregation of the negative emotions of the working class. It was presumably killed by Saitama. Appearance. Three-Eyed Ghost was a monster with a face that consisted of nothing more than three eyes and a mouth. Its body was entirely black with little to no detail and had four arms, two legs, and two horns. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapter. Salmon. Three-Eyed Ghost affects a man into committing suicide before he is saved by Saitama, it then starts openly attacking civilians. Abilities and Powers. Three-Eyed Ghost was a Tiger-level threat. After gathering the negative emotions of working people and growing to the size of a building, it was strong enough to destroy a building. Mind Control: It is said that whoever gets struck by the venomous breath of Three-Eyed Ghost loses self-consciousness and when they find themselves, they realize that they were planning their own suicide.

Tickle-Tickle Bug The Tickle-Tickle Bug (こちょこちょ虫, "Kocho-Kocho Mushi") is a small but deadly trick robot used by Child Emperor as a weapon. The robot's function is to aggressively and relentlessly tickle the target until they laugh to death from exhaustion and suffocation. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Child Emperor slips Tickle-Tickle Bug #3 through the gap in Phoenix Man's suit between his face and beak. Capabilities. Tickle-Tickle Bug is a robot intended to move within the clothes of the wearer. With its hands, it incessantly tickles the person, which provokes intense laughter. By this process, the person can suffer from asphyxiation.

Time Travel Time Travel is the ability to travel through time. Overview. The user is able to travel to the past or future. So far, this ability has only been used to travel to the past, with the only known users being Saitama and Garou. To accomplish this, one imagines their inner universe while manipulating the particles inside their body; when all of the particles inside their body turn into anti-particles, the user begins to travel backwards in time. During this process, the user enters a time tunnel where distorted "images" of past moments manifest before them. To choose a specific time and place to return to, the user simply traverses through the corresponding image, effectively transporting themselves to the desired temporal destination. Usage. Garou. After achieving his Cosmic Fear Mode, Garou gained the ability to manipulate particles within his body on a subatomic level and force them to behave like anti-particles. He refers to this power as the ultimate technique of his fist. However, Garou admitted that he hadn't yet mastered this technique for time travel. Nevertheless, there was an implication that he eventually did grab it. This was hinted at when Tareo was awakened by what appeared to be Garou's soul from the Ominous Future. The apparition slowly faded from view, suggesting that Garou had traversed time to bid farewell to the boy. Saitama. After being defeated by Saitama, Garou passed on to him his time travel technique in hope that Saitama could learn and master it in order to change the Ominous Future that occured during their fight. While executing his technique, Garou was soon killed by "God", who took back his powers in the process, although not before Saitama managed to replicate Garou's ability to time leap and use it to successfully travel to the past. Upon returning to the moment Garou was appearing in front of the heroes in Z-City, Saitama was able to defeat him with a single punch before any bad consequences could occur again, thus successfully changing the Ominous Future. However, right after this success, the "future" Saitama was forcibly pulled towards his "past" self in that timeline, resulting in a single Saitama with no memory of the Ominous Future and the time travel technique.

Timeline of Events This page is meant to catalog all major events in the "One-Punch Man" universe in chronological order. For a timeline of Webcomic events, please refer to Timeline of Events (webcomic).
Timeline of Events (webcomic) This page is meant to catalog all major events in the "One-Punch Man" universe in the original webcomic in chronological order.
To-do list A to-do list for the Wiki. If you are removing a task that has been completed, leave a note about its completion in the edit summary.

Tongara Tongara (トンガラ, "Tongara") was the captain of Narinki's Private Squad. He was fatally injured by Evil Natural Water and killed by Mad Doctor Fish. Appearance. Tonagara was a tall man with short black hair and an angular face, with a defined jaw and forehead. His battle attire consists of a specialized black and white power suit. Personality. Tongara was a level-headed and charismatic leader. He often wore a stoic and determined expression, but was no stranger to sly remarks and wit, and showed genuine fear for his life once captured by the Monster Association. Having witnessed so many atrocities on the battlefield (and committing some himself), Tongara had a nihilistic outlook. He believed that heroism and justice were lofty ideals, and that only money really mattered. He had a skewed moral compass, content to do anything that would get him ahead. However, after spending time with Atomic Samurai's disciples, Tongara found his optimism briefly regenerated. He even endangered his own life by saving Bushidrill from Evil Natural Water. In his final moments he admitted that it was brash to suddenly fancy himself a hero, and resigned to his fate as a nameless casualty. History. Few details are known about Tongara's past. As a member of a private military company, he had been a mercenary for many years before his role in Narinki's Private Squad, fighting in wars and black ops missions across the planet. During this time he saw just how rotten humanity can truly be. This led to him developing a morally apathetic outlook on life. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Tongara is appointed as the team leader of Narinki's Private Squad by Narinki to save his son from the Monster Association. Narinki states that if his squad retrieves his son, they will be paid very handsomely, so much so that even their grandchildren won't have to work. When Tongara and his team arrive at the hideout, they manage to kill two Mysterious Beings before being caught by G5 and brought before Orochi and Gyoro Gyoro. Tongara tearfully begs for mercy, explaining that he and his team were only in it for the money. Several monsters then jump to kill the mercenaries, but Royal Ripper stops them so he can have the pleasure of doing it himself. He then drags his blade across Tongara's face, creating an X shape. G5 intervenes, telling Gyoro Gyoro that their battle suits are potentially powerful weapons, so Do-S suggests to make them love slaves. Tongara and the mercenaries are then brainwashed into Do-S' servants by the strikes of her whip, putting their suits into overdrive. Before the Hero Association's invasion, Do-S orders Tongara and the others to each kill at least one hero. During the invasion, Do-S and the mercenaries come across Atomic Samurai's disciples and engage them in battle. Tongara's rifle is bisected by Iaian, forcing him to fight unarmed. Once Sweet Mask takes over for the three disciples, he moves to behead Tongara and the rest in one fell swoop - however, the disciples return and subdue them without any injuries. This also snaps Tongara out of Do-S' mind control, and he tearfully thanks Iaian. With Do-S defeated, Sweet Mask requests the disciples escort the mercenaries to the surface. Tongara and the mercenaries pretend to still be love slaves that had captured the three disciples, but when other monsters become interested they are forced to reveal themselves and fight. Afterwards, Tongara explains to Iaian that they are not leaving yet because they won't get paid unless they retrieve Waganma. It becomes clear that Tongara is not the heroic type, annoying Bushidrill. Impressed by Iaian's skills, Tongara offers him a position in his private military company, which he politely refuses. Tongara continues to pretend to be a love slave to get into the Monster Association's vault, but it still doesn't work and another fight breaks out. Noticing Master Joe escaping, Tongara splits up from his squad to pursue it alongside the disciples. He shoots Master Joe in an attempt to finish him off, but the monster still manages to pull the lever to release Evil Natural Water. Now trapped hiding from Evil Natural Water, Tongara attempts to shoot its eyeballs only to be pierced in the chest by its water cannons. Upon noticing it aiming for Bushidrill next, he rashly shoves him out of the way, taking the brunt of fire before being carried away by Iaian and Okamaitachi. Once separated from the monster by rubble, the disciples lay the mortally wounded Tongara down and he urges them to escape without him. As the light fades from his eyes, Tongara derisively laughs at his own stupidity, and his body is washed away in Evil Natural Water and devoured by Mad Doctor Fish. Abilities and Powers. As a member of Narinki's Private Squad equipped with new battle armor from The Organization, Tongara had impressive abilities. Together with the squad, he was able to pressure Atomic Samurai's disciples, who are S-Class material according to Fubuki. Mercenary skills. When not using weapons, Tongara was very proficient in close-quarter combat and seemed to use a variety of power-based attacks based on physical strength. His experience on the battlefield against enemy soldiers disguising themselves as civilians also developed his reflexes, allowing him to instantly counter attacks from behind. He could also create versatile strategies to deal with a variety of situations, but due to his lack of experience with monsters he was taken by surprise and his plan to rescue Waganma was ruined by Do-S and her brainwashing powers. As a professional mercenary, Tongara was also able to fake his emotions and trick others through acting, even though vicious monsters such as Royal Ripper are not easily affected by it. He was also able to replicate the behavior of a typical love slave of Do-S despite having experienced such a status only once. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Speed and Reflexes: As a trained mercenary, Tongara possessed superhuman speed and reflexes. This was shown when he managed to react to some of Evil Natural Water's high-speed jet streams, saving Bushidrill from the monster's deadly water bullets. Equipment. Battle Suit: Tongara wore armor manufactured by The Organization provided to him by Narinki. The armor is even more advanced than the previous battle suits and allows him to fight top-ranking A-Class heroes. Machine Gun: Tongara carried a machine gun with him and was relatively proficient in wielding it. The machine gun was destroyed by Iaian. Hand Gun: Tongara carried an emergency hand gun in case of need.

Tongue Stretcher Tongue Stretcher (シタノビール, "Shitanobīru") is a Mysterious Being that assaults beautiful women. Appearance. Tongue Stretcher is a chameleon-like mysterious being with large eyes, a tail, and a long tongue. Personality. Tongue Stretcher is a pervert that attacked young and beautiful women, wanting them to bear his children. However, when confronted by the strongest hero King, he surrendered and begged for mercy. History. Tongue Stretcher was a man with an intense love for reptiles that turned into the mysterious being known as the Tongue Stretcher. Plot. Hero Association Saga. King Arc. After becoming a Mysterious Being, the Tongue Stretcher attacked some girls to make them "bear his children". Before he could do anything, however, he met the S-Class hero King. Hearing the famous "King Engine" and fearing for his life, the Tongue Stretcher immediately admitted defeat and while begging for mercy he started to cry and shake. Tongue Stretcher is later seen on a prison bus with other Mysterious Beings who were captured by heroes. When the other Mysterious Beings ask who he was captured by, he replies that he was captured by King, at which the other Mysterious Beings immediately look up to him for surviving a battle with the strongest man. He points to a bruise on his head, which was actually caused by a woman stepping on him, as a mark of vendetta against King and swears vengeance, but never sees the light of day again. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. Tongue Stretcher manages to escape from the jail cell in the Hero Association Headquarters with Beer Bellee and Man-Eating Capybara thanks to Tatsumaki wrecking the place. The three of them soon confront a large group of heroes and immediately run away. Abilities and Powers. As a Wolf level threat, it can be assumed that Tongue Stretcher is a relatively weak Mysterious Being. Physical Abilities. Prehensile Tongue: Tongue Stretcher is able to elastically project his long tongue from his mouth at great speed. He has adhesive saliva on his tongue that causes his prey to get stuck to it. Enhanced Strength: Tongue Stretcher is strong enough to subdue five strong men with ease.

Torajirou Torajirou (トラヅロウ, "Torajirō") is the head judge at the Hero Costume Contest. Appearance. Torajirou is a middle aged man with his hair tied in a very wide ponytail and wears sunglasses. His attire is flamboyant wearing a business suit with polka dots with a white shirt underneath and a bow tie. He also wears a wristwatch and has pierced ears. Personality. Torajirou is a very judgmental man and gives harsh critique towards the costume contest. He judges peoples' personalities based on the clothes they wear and not as a person, scorning Saitama for his costume despite his own harsh character and lacking fashion sense. This later changes after his son confronted him about the clothes he gave him and decided to change the way he thinks. However, he is still quite ungrateful for Saitama in the end because of his wacky outfit while not seriously taking into account that Saitama did save his life from a monster. Nor accounting for his own horrendous tastes in clothing. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Sense. Torajirou is a head judge alongside Natalie Ver. 9 and Cleyopatra at the hero costume contest. He gives Darkness Blade a score of 2, telling him he is no good and should see himself more objectively so he wouldn't embarrass himself. While Saitama was the last contestant, he disregards Saitama's costume and judges his personality based on it. Just as he is about to give his score, Game-Berus attack the stadium, defeating other heroes and was about to attack the judges until Saitama step in and killed it with one punch. Despite Saitama saving the judges and gaining the audiences approval, he still didn't acknowledge the costume and gave him 1 point. After the contest ended, he spots his son at the stadium, questioning his outfit. Torao later explains that he doesn't like the clothes he gave and promoted his father to changes his view on other people. However, he still dislikes Saitama because of his clothing despite the fact Saitama saves his life.

Torako Torako (トラ子, "Torako") is the pet cat of a Hero Association staff member's daughter. Appearance. Torako is a small cat with white fur, yellow eyes and a blue collar. Personality. Torako was shown to be a caring mother to her children, as she was seen hunting and searching for food for them. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Lost Cat. Torako ran away from her owner and Saitama was asked by a Hero Association staff member to help find the cat. Torako was located at a restricted area where the monster Grizzly Nyah and her offspring were rampaging and many heroes fighting the Mysterious Beings. Torako refused her owners calls as she was rushing to her kittens that were in the bush. Grizzly Nyah corners Torako and as the cat hisses, Saitama defends her from the monster. Saitama then saves Torako from the monster and reunites her with her owner. As Saitama picks up Torako, she scratches him, and Saitama threatens to punch her.

Torako's Owner An unnamed little girl who is the owner of the cat Torako and the daughter of a staff member of the Hero Association. Appearance. She is a small girl with dark-colored eyes and dark, wavy hair tied in a ponytail with her fringe partly covering her forehead. She wears a jacket over her striped shirt, a frilly skirt, short leggings and sneakers. Personality. She is a bratty child and tends to repeat herself and threatens to tell on Saitama, but when the latter didn't care she starts to cry. She loves her cat Torako very much, worrying about her whereabouts and was happy to take her kittens with her. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Lost Cat. She tags along with Saitama to help her find her cat Torako. She then draws a picture of her cat to help Saitama, but the bald hero is only stumped by the drawing. Annoyed by his statement, she threatens to get him fired, but is surprised by the lack of care and begins to cry, which prompts Saitama to comfort her. They continue to search for her cat and come towards an isolated area guarded by Tanktop Tiger and Tanktop Black Hole. When they are told that only chosen heroes may go beyond that point, Saitama states that that may count him as well. As they are searching in the isolated area, Genos breaks through the wall, while fighting Grizzly Nyah, frightening her. Saitama happens to notice a cat that matches the description and continues with their search. She finds Torako and begins to chase her, but is caught by Stinger and Lightning Genji who were running away from the mother Grizzly Nyah. After Saitama kills the monster, she is reunited with her cat and is excited to know that she gave birth to two small kittens.

Torao Torao (トラオ, "Torao") is the son of the fashion police Torajirou. Appearance. Torao is a young boy with short black hair that is parted to the left. He used to wear very tacky clothes made by his father, but later started wearing a normal, more simple outfit. Personality. Torao was bullied quite a lot, because of the tacky dresses his father made him wear, but after meeting Saitama he stood up to him and started to wear what he likes. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapters. Sense. He was crying outside the stadium where the hero costume contest was held in his underwear. When asked, he told Saitama and Genos about how the bullies took his clothes. Saitama gave him his outfit and told him to go home. After the contest, he found Saitama and returned his hero costume, thanking him. He arrived at the stadium to see his father, only to tell him the outfits he gave him were horrible and he will wear what he likes.
Torgeva Torgeva (ドルゲバ, "Dorugeba") is the Hero Association's Sales Division, Planning and Design Section Toy Designer.

Toupee Warrior Toupee Warrior (ヅラ戦士, "Zura Senshi") is the C-Class Rank 83 professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. Toupee Warrior is a man with a noticeably large head of hair, which is assumed to be a toupée. He wears a sweater with zig-zag patterns all along it and a pair of shorts. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Toupee Warrior is part of the Hero Name Victims Association, and goes with them to request Saitama to join them. He is later seen protesting with the rest of the group outside the Hero Association's executive meeting room. His "Desired Name" is Gold Kneed Warrior.

Training Monsterbot Training Monsterbot is a non-canon character who serves a purpose as a fighting tutorial in "". Appearance. The Training Monsterbot is a bald robot that resembles with grey skin, an emotionless expression on his face. Along with goggles for eyes and headponhes with a speaker over his head. He resembles Genos clothing wise and has similar arms. Description. The Training Monsterbot is a training bot owned by the Hero Association, specialised in training new heroes how to fight. He is the first fight and mission of the game and shows the battle mechanics to the Custom Hero in order to progress.

Transformation Transformation is the ability to transform parts of one body which usually comes with a significant boost in power and/or speed. Overview. A human or animal can undergo a normally irreversible transformation into a Mysterious Being by different means: Several Mysterious Beings possess the ability to transform; morphing into an alternate, more powerful form. Some Mysterious Beings that have high willpower possess the ability to transform back and forth between monster and human forms, although in some cases this requires a great deal of training, as seen with the ninjutsu training Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame went through. Only Surprise-Attack Plum, Gale Wind, Hellfire Flame and Haragiri are known to have this ability. Puri-Puri Prisoner refers to his "Angel Style" as a transformation, as he significantly increases his muscle mass, a side effect of which his clothes get torn off. It is also possible for someone to become a half-monster through brainwashing such as humans who had been captured by and forced under Do-S' command. Though upon regaining their identities and being released from the brainwashing, their monsterization features soon go away as Bang theorizes unlike most Mysterious Beings, the captured humans hearts weren't obsessed and thus they cannot be considered true monsters. Types. Several of the House of Evolution's mutants possess unique transformation abilities. Mosquito Girl is able to undergo a Metamorphosis (変身, "Henshin") upon obtaining enough blood and Carnage Kabuto can undergo a transformation into Carnage Mode (阿修羅モード, "Ashura Mōdo"). The Deep Sea King of the Seafolk takes on a dry form when out of the sea for too long, but will return to his hydrated form with enough water. The alien Boros is able to utilize Power Release (パワー解放, "Pawā kaihō") upon the removal of his armor to transform, and after releasing this power he can transform once more using Meteoric Burst (メテオリックバースト, "Meteorikku Bāsuto"). Under the right circumstances, Centipede monsters (such as Elder Centipede) possess the ability to transform via Molting (脱皮, "Dappi"); increasing their size, granting additional armor and giving them an extra face. Through his shape-changing box, the cybernetic hero Drive Knight is able to undergo a Tactical Transformation (戦術変形, "Senjutsu Henkei") into a variety of different forms The Monster King Orochi has a great amount of control over his body. He is normally in a humanoid form but is also able to transform his body into his "released form" composed of snake-like dragons, teeth, and claws. He can also condense himself into a slimmer humanoid form with his horns shapeshifting into dragons. With each Resurrection, Phoenix Man gained the ability to take on new forms, with his first resurrection he took on a permanent state which raised his disaster level from Demon to Dragon and allowed him to utilize.

Trap Tengu Trap Tengu (罠天狗, "Wana Tengu") is the B-Class Rank 70 professional hero for the Hero Association. Appearance. Trap Tengu's costume is modeled after his . He wears a (which resembles the face of a bird), a wig, traditional garb (including a ), and . He also carries an oibako (wooden backpack) containing his various traps. Appearances in Other Media. Omakes. Squadron. Trap Tengu was summoned by the Hero Association along with Pink Hornet, Wild Horn, Smell Master and Saitama, to capture a Scaledon alive for medical research. When the heroes reached the woods, Wild Horn ordered Tengu to place traps to snare the monster. Scaledon fell into the trap, but managed to break free and swallow all of the heroes. In the end, Saitama punched the monster, saving Tengu and the others. Abilities and Powers. As a B-Class hero, Trap Tengu is a fairly skilled fighter. Though based on his rank, he isn't very strong by B-Class standards. As his name suggests, he is very skilled with traps. Fighting Style. Expert Trapper: Trap Tengu uses traps to fight his opponents. Equipment. Traps: Trap Tengu has a large array of traps that can be used against opponents.

Triple Tongues The Triple Tongues (三枚舌, "Sanmai Shita") were a group of Mysterious Beings. Appearance. The Triple Tongues appeared to be normal humans. The only differences being that they each had three long tongues and sharp teeth. Personality. Not much is known about their personalities. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. They are first seen fighting against Crescent Eyebroll, who is struggling and unable to deal any damage to them because of their numbers and attack range. As he tries to escape and wait for support, Ryumon and his gang appear to save Crescent Eyebroll. The Ryumon Gang then swiftly deal with the Triple Tongues. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about the Triple Tongues. Given that they were a Tiger-level threat, it can be assumed that they were a fairly strong group. They were powerful enough to easily overwhelm the A-Class hero, Crescent Eyebroll, and the hero stated that they were more trouble than their Tiger disaster level suggested. Fighting Style. The Triple Tongues rely almost entirely on their tongues to strike, stab, and grab their opponents from a safe distance. It seems that they are weak in close quarters combat as they lost quickly to the Ryumon Gang after they had closed the distance on them.

Tsukuyomi Tsukuyomi (ツクヨミ, "Tsukuyomi") is a psychic research organization that experimented on Tatsumaki when she was a little girl. Overview. Tsukuyomi has been researching psychic power and claimed that it is for the advancement of humanity. Members of this organization consist of scientists who have done many experiments on Tatsumaki. They have at least one research facility. They appear to have been producing artificial espers. History. In the past, when Tatsumaki was only seven years old, this organization discovered her psychic powers and took her away from her adoptive parents, giving them money in exchange. They did notice a two-year-old Fubuki as well, but decided to let her be because unlike Tatsumaki, she had not yet developed her own psychic abilities. For the next 3 years, Tatsumaki was held and experimented on at a research facility run by Tsukuyomi. During this time, a hybrid monster broke free and began rampaging through the facility. As people fled, Tatsumaki was locked in a cell, pretending she couldn't use her powers. When the monster approached her cell, Blast arrived and killed the monster, rescuing Tatsumaki. Once free, Tatsumaki went off to go to Fubuki, with Tsukuyomi becoming aware of this and trying to retrieve her. After meeting Fubuki, Tatsumaki was ambushed by four Tsukuyomi agents who presumably got killed by her soon afterward. A child Fubuki witnessed this and became scared of her older sister. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. After the Monster Association is defeated, the Tsukuyomi learns that the Hero Association had captured Psykos. The Tsukuyomi offers a large sum of money to the Hero Association in exchange for Psykos, and being low on both funds and morality, they accept. The Tsukuyomi then sends an agent called Apollo to collect Psykos. When Apollo arrives, he is escorted to her cell where he refers to Psykos as a "sample" that would bring a great leap in research progress for them. It is also revealed that the Tsukuyomi somehow knew about Psykos's "third eye" ability to see into the future and would research it with a thorough craniotomy. Tatsumaki and Fubuki were aware of the Tsukuyomi and intercept Apollo. He is greatly outmatched by Tatsumaki, but manages to turn the tables and almost capture the two of them and Psykos for research. His attempt to capture them fails, but he manages to escape along with another unnamed Tsukuyomi agent who was undercover in the Blizzard Group. Later, Eyelashes, Lily, and Needle Star confront the two Hero Association executives who escorted Apollo to Psykos's cell. Eyelashes questions their supposed ignorance about Tsukuyomi, given they were in such a remote location. In response, they claim to have been there during their free time. Gearsper notices the conversation and defends the executives. He states that "Tsukuyomi" is the name of a long-lasting urban legend among espers, and that the scheme was based on a ridiculous rumor. He then suggests that the attempt to retrieve Psykos was probably made by survivors from the Monster Association, under the guise of a trade-off.

Tsukuyomi Spy An unnamed Tsukuyomi agent who was undercover in the Fubuki Group and is an artificial Esper. Appearance. He is a young man with an undercut curtains hairstyle that raises when he flies revealing a scar on the left side of his head. He wears large earrings and Fubuki Group attire. History. At some point in the past (most likely quite recently), he was accepted into the Fubuki Group. While there he collected intelligence. He might be the reason why the Tsukuyomi knew about Tatsumaki's fight with Psykos, and Psykos's "third eye" ability. He also managed to slip a poison capsule into Fubuki's daily beauty supplements. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. After Apollo captures the psychic sisters and Psykos, the Tsukuyomi Spy reveals himself and prepares to depart with him as to not be killed by the demon level monsters Apollo released. After revealing himself, Mountain Ape refers to him as "the new guy". When Tatsumaki defeats Apollo, he attempts to escape through a hole but is forcefully slammed into the wall next to it. Later, when Saitama and Tatsumaki are arguing and go outside to fight, he and Apollo tunnel underground into the parking lot where Apollo's car is. Since Apollo is badly wounded, he takes the wheel and drives off. He asks if Apollo is alright, and notices a large tornado in the rear view mirror, wondering if it was Tatsumaki. Abilities and Powers. Supernatural Abilities. Psychokinesis: Being a Tsukuyomi agent and artificial Esper, he has some amount of telekinetic capability. Flight: He can move himself telekinetically at some magnitude of speed. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Durability: He was able to survive being slammed into a concrete wall at a speed that caused it to crack and crumble around him.

TurtleBerus Game-Berus (ガメベロス, "Gameberosu"; Viz: GameBeros) was a Mysterious Being who attacked the first Hero Costume Contest. It was killed by Saitama. Appearance. Game-Berus was a giant sentient turtle-like creature who had three heads and a shell, characterised by a muddy green-ish color. It could stand on its hind legs. History. Game-Berus was originally a turtle. When its owner flushed it down the toilet, into the sewers, it transformed into a monster after bathing in sewage. Personality. Not much is known about it, but it seemed determined to drown humans in sewer water. Appearances in Other Media. Extra Chapter. Sense. Game-Berus interrupts a hero costume contest before Saitama can get a final verdict. After easily defeating B-Class and C-Class heroes, it declares that it will drown humans in sewer water. It is then defeated by a punch from Saitama after charging at the judges. Power and Abilities. As a Demon-level threat, Game-Berus was quite powerful. A group of C and B-Class heroes were unable to do anything against it and the S-Class hero Genos even praised the monster after Saitama killed it, remarking that Game-Berus wasn't weak. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Durability: Game-Berus had a very tough shell and skin, as the B-Class hero Darkness Blade was not able to deal any damage to it. Enhanced Strength: Game-Berus had enough strength to effortlessly smack aside various C and B-Class heroes, including Darkness Blade whose armor was easily broken with a single hit. Spherical Form: Game-Berus could roll into a ball to attack others with greater speed and power than his regular strikes.

Twin-Headed Tsuchinoko Twin-Headed Tsuchinoko (双頭ツチノコ, "Sōtō Tsuchinoko") was a Demon-level threat that resided under the Hero Association headquarters prison. It was killed by Saitama. Appearance. Twin-Headed Tsuchinoko was a worm-like monster with two heads and very sharp teeth with no eyes. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Psychic Sisters Arc. During Tatsumaki's and Fubuki's battle, they damage the area around them, causing Twin-Headed Tsuchinoko to escape prison. The monster senses Saitama and tries to attack him, but Saitama simply grabs the monster and smashes it into the ground, opening an underground prison of monsters. Abilities and Powers. Not much is known about its powers, though given its disaster level of Demon, Twin-Headed Tsuchinoko was presumably very powerful.

Twin Tail Twin Tail (ツインテール, "Tsuintēru") is an A-Class professional hero of the Hero Association. Appearance. As her name suggests, Twin Tail has a pigtail hairstyle with four dice holding together each tail. Each die has four on all sides, which rhymes with death in Japanese. She dresses like a jester and wears a blindfold, she also has a teardrop painted on her cheek; as to why remains unclear. Personality. Although not much is known about Twin Tail's personality, she is very confident as well as rather morbid. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Twin Tail is one of the heroes recruited to the Monster Association raid's support team. As they enter the abandoned district, she picks up the breaths of monsters all around the heroes and informs the others that they're surrounded. She defeats several monsters with her Death Loop. She is nearly killed by a Monster Association sniper, but gets saved by One Shotter. When Rhino Wrestler appears to battle the heroes, she is one of the several who attempts to fight the monster, but is easily knocked back, with the monster rating her attack a 9 out of 100. After Rhino Wrestler is killed by Atomic Samurai and the rest of the S-Class heroes eliminate the remaining monsters, she stays above ground with he rest of the support squad while the strike team infiltrates the Monster Association headquarters. After eliminating several escaping low-class monsters, Twin Tail is cut down by the Monster Association executive Nyan along with several other members of the support team, his attack being too fast for them to see. Abilities and Powers. As an A-Class hero, Twin Tail is a skilled and powerful fighter. Despite wearing a blindfold, Twin Tail is skilled at fighting and is able to sense presences of Mysterious Beings around her with her augmented senses. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: As one of the A-Class heroes, Twin Tail naturally has impressive strength, and uses it to wield her multiple weapons and cut apart her enemies. Enhanced Speed & Reflexes: Being an A-Class hero, Twin Tail has very impressive speed and is able to dispatch multiple monsters in a short period of time. Enhanced Senses: One of Twin Tail's most impressive traits as a hero are her heightened senses. Since she constantly wears a blindfold, Twin Tail's other senses are extremely augmented, perhaps the most impressive senses in the series. Some examples of her unbelievable senses are when she is able to hear the breathing of monsters from every direction and being able to juggle multiple pins, balls and scimitars without even looking at them. Fighting Style. Juggle: Twin Tail juggles her multiple accessories popped out of her suit which she uses to kill monsters.

Typhoon Family No. 2 Man The unnamed man is the Typhoon Family's Number 2 man. Appearance. He is a tall man with a pale complexion with his silver hair combed back. He has sunken cheeks and light green eyes. He wears a long white trench coat with black lining a black gloves. Personality. He seemed to be a sickly man and has some rivalry with Don Pacino. Appearances in Other Media. OVA. The Pupil Who Is an Extremely Poor Talker. Genos finds the man, asking him about the closed supermarket. The man informs Genos that this is the work of Don Pacino, before collapsing in front of him. Moments later Don Pacino appears and takes the man hostage and questioning Genos about his connection with him. In the end Genos promptly defeats the Pacino Family and saves the man.
U-City U-City (U市 "U Shi") is a very large city situated on the Earth. Nothing much is known about this city. There are 30 heroes living in this city. Inhabitants. Heroes. Number of Heroes by Class:

Ugmons Ugmons (ブサモン, "Busamon") are an unusual type of Mysterious Beings created from ugly humans. Overview. Ugmons are formerly ugly humans, who have become monsters due to bullying, or from being turned down by the opposite sex. The feelings of jealousy or inferiority turn into hatred, covering their hearts with darkness dyed with evil. Their strength after turning into monsters is influenced by the hideousness of their hearts. They seem to be common knowledge as the kids bullying Tareo mention their existence. They are able to grow in size and rearrange their body parts.

Ultimate Premium Beef Gift Set Ultimate Premium Beef Gift Set is a packet of exceptionally high quality beef that Dr. Kuseno gives to Saitama as a gift for taking care of Genos. The gift is hard to come by and Dr. Kuseno heard that Saitama reacts to bargain sale beef at the supermarket. Saitama decides to use it in a hotpot, much to Fubuki's disappointment, as she thinks he shouldn't waste such a high quality product for some simple hotpot. When Saitama was hesitant about spending time in a machine to measure his physical specifications, Kuseno offered high quality beef in which they barbequed and ate together.

Underdog Man Underdog Man (カマセイヌマン, "Kamaseinu Man") is a series of robots created by Child Emperor. They assist Child Emperor in battle. Appearance. The robots of the Underdog Man series appear as dog-like humanoid robots. They can be easily mistaken for real heroes. When 3 Underdog Men combine they take on the appearance of a three-headed muscular humanoid beast. Each head has a spiky collar which is tied together with chains and a belt. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Child Emperor uses it to fight the monster Eyesight and to save the poisoned heroes. After being bitten by Eyesight's poisonous snakes, Child Emperor collects the data and sends it to the Hero Association to create an antidote. Underdog Man No. 22 then grabs Eyesight and self destructs. Monster Association Arc. Underdog Man No. 23, No. 24 and No. 25 are deployed to battle G5. They combine into their more powerful form and fight G5. With Child Emperor's pencil missiles, the hero buys enough time for him and Waganma to escape. No. 23, No. 24 and No. 25 are his last remaining Underdog Man robots. Abilities and Powers. As individuals, the Underdog Men are somewhat powerful, and one Underdog Man is capable of holding its own against Eyesight until activating its self-destruct. When three Underdog Men combined to form Mad Dog Underdog Cerberus, the new robot's power is formidable, although G5 was able to destroy it without incurring any noticeable damage. Dog Paddle Punch (犬かきパンチ, "Inukaki Panchi"): Underdog Man jumps at its opponent. The full effect of this technique is unknown, as it wasn't able to connect to its target. Self Destruct: Underdog Man jumps at its opponent and destroys itself with a powerful explosion. Mad Dog: Underdog Cerberus (狂犬 カマセケルベロス, "Kyōken Kamase Keruberosu"): Three Underdog Men can combine into a new powerful form.Although it's true power is unknown, as the battle between it and G5 wasn't shown, G5 felt it necessary to unsheath a second katana. An unseen battle took place, and G5 managed to defeat Mad Dog Underdog Cerberus without any apparent injuries.

Unihorn Unihorn (イッカク, "Ikkaku") was a Demon-level monster and a member of the Monster Association. He was one of the monsters sent by Gyoro Gyoro to investigate an unknown intruder, along with Super Mouse and Showerhead.. He was killed by Overgrown Rover. Appearance. Unihorn was a humanoid creature with a large horn as a forehead. He had eyes all over his body; malformed teeth, misaligned jaws and no apparent nose or ears. In his transformed state, Unihorn took on the shape of a long lance and his mouth moved to the center of the shaft. Eyes appeared on the linings of his body in both states. Personality. As a monster, he naturally seemed to be confident in himself, proclaiming his horn as "the hardest in the world," and "unbreakable." Unlike many other monsters in the association, he was willing to work alongside other monsters to fight other opponents. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Association Arc. Unihorn appears alongside his partners, Super Mouse and Showerhead, to confront Garou. Unihorn says Garou is full of himself, and proceeds to attack him first, swinging his body around like a giant buzzsaw. However, Garou easily anticipates his move and sends him crashing to the wall. While Super Mouse and Showerhead distracted Garou, Unihorn transforms into his killer form. Super Mouse picks him up for their combo move, the Demon Trinity Bursting Speed Thrust. Unfortunately for them, Garou had already experienced a similar attack against Stinger and deflects it. Alas, Garou forgot that Overgrown Rover was still standing behind them, and the attack caused him to deem all of the people in the room as threats. Overgrown Rover tosses back Unihorn, who, despite boasting of an "unbreakable horn", is broken. He is then vaporized by Rover's energy blast alongside his partners. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level threat, Unihorn was a very powerful monster. He managed to survive an attack from an evolving Garou. However, against Dragon-level monsters, he was utterly helpless, as he was effortlessly broken apart by Overgrown Rover. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: Being a Demon-level mysterious being, it can be presumed that Unihorn had impressive physical strength. Enhanced Speed: Unihorn was rather fast, being fast enough to spin himself around at intense speeds, appearing as a giant circular saw. Enhanced Durability: Unihorn proclaimed to have an "unbreakable horn", and was also strong enough to take a kick from Garou unharmed. However, he was easily defeated and mangled by Overgrown Rover, while in his transformed state. Killer Form (必殺形態, "Hissatsu Keitai"; Viz: Killingest Form): Unihorn could transform his humanoid body into a sharpened spear. While in this state he lost his arms and legs but had a longer reach. This form was used in a combination attack with Showerhead and Super Mouse who shot him at a high speed. Fighting Style. Slice and Pierce: Unihorn's attack revolved around stabbing and cutting his opponents. Trivia. Unihorn's name and his transformation are a reference to the narwhal, a cetacean with a very long horn-shaped tusk. In fact, the Japanese name イッカク ("Ikkaku") literally means "one horn", but generally means "narwhal".

Unnamed Lightning Demon An unnamed Demon-level threat. It was killed by Mumen Rider. Appearance. This monster was huge and muscular with horns coming out of its head and back that looked like to be bolts of lightning. It had two eyes and no mouth. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. Stinger, Blue Fire and a small group of Neo Heroes are seen defeated on the ground, saying that the monster is too powerful for them to handle. People are terrified as it was able to defeat A Class Heroes, while the monster is heading towards a mother and her children. Mumen Rider shows up to confront the monster. It looks to be defeating him with ease, using his powerful arms and shooting lighting at him. It's revealed Satoru has a battle suit, and through his determination, he is finally able to overpower the monster and kill it with Justice Uppercut. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level threat, it was a powerful monster, being able to defeat A-Class heroes and Neo heroes with apparent ease. It also had the ability to manipulate lightning. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: It appeared to have great physical strength, showing to defeat A-Class heroes with no effort. It was also able to punch through solid concrete with ease. Supernatural Abilities. Electricity Manipulation: As an electricity-based monster, it has shown the ability to change the weather, making the clouds go dark and generate lightning. It can also shoot lightning at its opponents.

Unnamed Warrior of the dragon alliance One of the nine warriors of the Dragon Alliance who's name was never said. Appearance. A Mysterious Being who has black spiked hair and is quite muscular, he also wears a black Gi to indicate he might know some form of martial art. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Neo Heroes Introduction Arc. This Mysterious Being had obtained one of the nine sealing orbs in an attempt to summon the Cruel Dragon, though was quickly planted head first into a wall by Saitama. Maybe if Saitama spoke to him about his intentions there wouldn't have been a need to fight, though he attacked Saitama without hearing him out first.

Urn Eel Urn Eel (オモウツボ, "Omoutsubo") was a Tiger-level Mysterious Being and a Seafolk. He was killed by Puri-Puri Prisoner. Appearance. Urn Eel was a large eel-like creature. He stood upright, his body extending from the inside of a white and purple urn. He possessed brown scales, webbed arms and legs, and a large mouth full of sharp teeth. Appearances in Other Media. OVAs. Puri-Puri Prisoner and the Jailbreaking Prisoners. Urn Eel was part of the Seafolk's invasion of the surface world. After the invasion was stopped by the Hero Association, Urn Eel managed to escape and live in hiding. Urn Eel had set up a hideout in an abandoned house in the countryside. Several escaped inmates from Smelly Lid Prison hid in the house while he was away. Once he returned, Urn Eel decided to eat all of them for intruding but was stopped by the arrival of Puri-Puri Prisoner, who easily defeated him. Urn Eel stood back up for round two, refusing to be beaten by a pervert, but was killed anyway. Abilities and Powers. As a Tiger-level monster, it can be assumed that Urn Eel was fairly powerful. His fighting style is unknown, due to how quickly Puri-Puri Prisoner dispatched him.

V-City V-City (V市, "V Shi") is a large city situated on the Earth. There are 16 heroes living in this city. Inhabitants. Heroes. Number of Heroes by Class: Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. During the Monster Raid, Pureblood attacks V-City.

Vaccine Man Vaccine Man (ワクチンマン, "Wakuchin Man") was a Mysterious Being supposedly born from the release of excessive pollution and waste generated by the industries made by human beings. He claimed he was created as an incarnation of nature's wrath and was tasked to wipe out humanity and thus effectively "vaccinate" the Earth against future "infections." He was killed by Saitama. Appearance. Vaccine Man was a large, purple hairless humanoid with two rounded antennae on his head. He had a bare muscular body. Vaccine Man also demonstrated the ability of shapeshifting, he could transform into a bigger and complex form, armed with large teeth, claws, and fangs. Personality. Acting as the anti-villain antagonist, Vaccine Man set out to extinguish humanity for the sake of his interpretation on the status of the environment being poor, as he considered humans to be an "infection" that wither the environment into a polluted, tainted mess of machinery; and carcasses of organisms. The thought of opposition enraged him for he believed he acted out the wishes of planet Earth. History. Vaccine Man was supposedly created as a response to the industrial reign over nature. Conceived by nature, in his own words, he has been formed to serve as the apostle of Mother Earth and under the wishes of such. He believes the Earth as a single living organism that is in need of protection and relief of pain, so Vaccine Man has set out to carry out the deed in extinguishing humanity so nature can prosper completely once more. To do this, he has tasked himself to attack the areas where humans are known to live in an infrastructure of technology and artificial order. Plot. Introduction Saga. Vaccine Man appears next to A-City, creating a crater as a result of his travels. He conceives multiple balls of energy that cause further destruction to the city. Lightning Max and Smile Man were sent after Vaccine Man but are defeated easily. He then notices a crying schoolgirl and proceeds to try to grab and crush her. She is saved by Saitama, whom Vaccine Man questions regarding the hero's identity. Saitama says that he is just an average hero doing average hero things as a hobby. Offended at Saitama's casual attitude, Vaccine Man launches into a diatribe about his name and purpose while transforming into his second form. Saitama quickly defeats him in a single punch, the staple of the latter's heroic deeds for the rest of the series. Credit for defeating him ultimately went to King, who was passing by and accidentally tripped onto Vaccine Man’s remains. Appearances in Other Media. Video Games. Vaccine Man is a playable character in the video game, "One Punch Man: A Hero Nobody Knows". Abilities and Powers. Vaccine Man was a creature of great strength and size, enough so to be classed a threat level of "Dragon." He could destroy a large part of a big city quickly. He breezed through 31 heroes, some of which included passing by a couple A-Class heroes and making them retreat without even noticing them. He was also said to be perhaps the greatest mysterious being that appeared till that point in time. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: As a Dragon-level Mysterious Being, Vaccine Man was presumably very powerful, although the depths of his strength were never seen. He was strong enough to defeat two A-Class heroes and several other heroes with apparently little to no effort. Transformation (変身, "Henshin"): Vaccine Man can transform into his true, more advanced form, bearing longer claws & teeth, a darker coloration, solid luminescent red eyes, tusks, and scales and spikes. He can even revert just one part of his body to preserve energy, as was shown when he was about to crush a schoolgirl. Supernatural Abilities. Energy Balls (エネルギー弾, "Enerugī-dan"): Vaccine Man was capable of shooting energy balls which caused large-scale explosions upon cities. His energy balls are said to be the accumulation of "biological" energy present naturally on Earth. Flight (飛行能力, "Hikō nōryoku"): Despite not having any wings, Vaccine Man possesses the ability to fly. When he does, he is surrounded by an aura that's similar to his energy balls and takes off several feet in the air.
Valkyrie Connect Valkyrie Connect is a that has a tie-in event featuring the "One-Punch Man" series.

Vampire (Pureblood) Vampire (Pureblood) (バンパイア (血統書付), "Banpaia (Kettōsho Tsuki)", Viz: Vampire (pedigreed)) was a Demon-level Mysterious Being and a member of the Monster Association. He was killed by Zombieman. Appearance. He was a vampire monster with slanted eyes, pointy teeth, and light-colored hair combed back and long sideburns reaching his chest. His attire consisted of black pants, a gray double-breasted vest with two chains, puffed shoulders, a ruffled collar, and a white shirt. Over this, he donned a long black cape. Personality. He was a cruel, merciless, and arrogant vampire that came from an ancient bloodline of vampires. Due to his noble upbringing, he viewed all the monsters around him as fakes, and hates being around them, often stating that he is the only "true monster" among the entire Association. He would often target weaker monsters of the Monster Association as food sources. Because of this violent attitude, many monsters viewed him with disdain, and all of the monsters that watched the battle between Pureblood and Zombieman were ready to come together and eliminate Pureblood if he won the fight and was in a weakened state for them to exploit. He was also shown to be rather haughty, completely self-assured of his own greatness and everyone else's failures. In his pedigree as a true, blue monster compared to the rest of the herd, he believed that after dealing with the heroes the time would come when he would dispatch Orochi as King of Monsters, as well as all of the other creatures and Mysterious Beings whom he considered to be fakes. This was in spite of not taking up the challenge issued by Gyoro Gyoro to battle the Monster Association's leader at the time when he'd dispatched Awakened Cockroach for his failure, and showed some cowardice behind his bluster and racism. He also possessed a condescending attitude towards humans and non-human humanoids such as Zombieman. This is displayed when he bitterly mocked the immortal hero for his human origin and how he lacks any semblance of humanity due to his unique conditioning. This, coupled with his high narcissism gave Pureblood the notion that he stood above such an inferior race whose only real talent was using cheap tactics to compensate for their lack of anything resembling ability. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Pureblood and many other monsters from the Monster Association all attack random cities simultaneously. Pureblood quickly massacres a good portion of the population of V-City. Monster Association Arc. Pureblood is shown at the Monster Association base, where he sucks another monster dry while conversing with a turtle-like Mysterious Being. After that, he proclaims that he cowers before Orochi only to defeat the Hero Association and he is truly the most powerful monster since he is the descendant of ancient vampire lineage. He is mildly annoyed by Devil Long Hair, who states he got his monster transformation from grooming his long hair, something Pureblood finds ridiculous. Pureblood, along with the rest of the monsters, prepare to fight the intruders when the Hero Association attacks. Sometime later, when other monsters are fighting Zombieman, the monsters guide them to a room, where Pureblood is hanging from the ceiling. The other monsters crowd in, eager to see which one of them survives and planning to feast on the weakened victor. Zombieman asks why all of the other monsters are planning to gang up on Pureblood, and he responds by saying they're envious of his power. Pureblood states his intention to kill the other monsters when he's done and asks Zombieman who he is. Zombieman begins an introduction but quickly draws his two pistols and fires at Pureblood. However, the vampire managed to appear behind Zombieman and bites him on his carotid artery. Surprisingly, Pureblood recoils, disgusted by the hero's surprisingly terrible tasting blood. Zombieman gets back on his feet, while Pureblood, believing Zombieman to be using the last of his strength to stand, regales the hero with his history as the strongest, and only, natural monster in the Monster Association, being a part of a hereditary lineage of vampires. Zombieman reloads his pistols with more powerful bullets and fires at Pureblood, although the force of the ammo manages to break both of Zombieman's arms. Pureblood throws the bullets back at Zombieman, although he's surprised when he sees Zombieman still standing. He realizes that Zombieman is the undying S-class hero he'd heard of. The fight resumes, but Pureblood quickly finds his own regeneration outmatched by Zombieman's. Thirty minutes later, Zombieman stands victoriously over Pureblood's bloody corpse with dead bats lying all around. The dying vampire is shocked and confused at how the hero managed to still stand, even after he'd killed him so many times. Zombieman tells the unresponsive Pureblood that he gave him about two hundred lethal wounds. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level Mysterious Being of the Monster Association, Pureblood was a very powerful being. It took Zombieman, an S-Class hero, over 30 minutes to defeat him, with the hero noting that Pureblood gave Zombieman about 200 lethal wounds that would take about 3 minutes to completely recover. The hero also noted the Vampire was the strongest monster he fought in a while. Pureblood, by his own account, is the strongest natural monster in the Monster Association due to his ancient vampire lineage. Physical Abilities. Enhanced Strength: Given his status as a Demon-level monster, Pureblood was a naturally strong being. He was strong enough to easily rip apart a human body and a monster's body, as well as break Zombieman's neck with a single kick. He was also strong enough to throw the bullets he caught from Zombieman's Desert Eagle back with enough velocity to pierce the hero's brain. Enhanced Speed and Agility: Pureblood was fast enough to easily catch bullets and rips vital organs from a human's body before they could notice. He was also able to outpace the S-Class hero Zombieman several times during their battle, and was even nimble enough to land perfectly on the tip of Zombieman's sword. Blood Consumption: As a vampire, Pureblood had a natural affinity for draining and metabolizing the hemoglobin of other sentient creatures for sustenance. This was not limited to human beings, but other monsters as well. He often targeted weaker monsters of the Monster Association to drain their blood. Transformation: Pureblood could freely transform his body into a colony of vampire bats, which could attack as a swarm. He could also transform a sleeve of his clothes into a sharp blade.

Vampires Vampires are a natural type of mysterious beings. Overview. Vampires are natural mysterious beings. They are not born through artificial methods such as monster cells. All vampires have the ability to drain the blood from living creatures such as humans and organic mysterious beings. Vampires do not seem to be affected by sunlight as Pureblood was attacking in broad daylight unaffected.

Venus Mantrap Venus Mantrap (ヒトトリグサ, "Hitotorigusa", Viz: Venus Peopletrap) was a Mysterious Being that attacks Narinki, the sponsor of the Hero Association with Junior Centipede. He was killed by Metal Bat. Appearance. Venus Mantrap was a big monster with the appearance of a carnivorous plant. Personality. His personality was left rather ambiguous, but he seemed to be rather impatient and lusted for human flesh. Plot. Human Monster Saga. Monster Raid Arc. Venus Mantrap emerges from the ground with Junior Centipede at a restaurant. Junior Centipede briefly mentions that he is looking for the sponsor of Hero Association. Before they could grab the sponsor, Metal Bat grabs a coat and engages in a fight with him and his partner. Venus Mantrap's corpse is being sat upon by Metal Bat. A heavily injured Junior Centipede notes that Metal Bat killed Venus Mantrap in an instant.

Vibrating Tremor Vibrating Tremor (震動のヴァイブ, "Shindō no Vaibu") is a ninja from the Ninja Village. He is from the 19th graduating class, and a member of the Heavenly Ninja Party. Appearance. Vibrating Tremor was a pleasant-looking man with a babyface. He wore a button-up sweater and pants. History. Vibrating Tremor graduated from the 19th class of the Ninja Village known as "Momentum," like Instant Moment. He later joined the Heavenly Ninja Party.
Video Game-Only Characters "For a list of all other characters, see Characters". <tabber> Games= </tabber>

Villains Villains and Criminals are individuals, usually human, that disturb the normal functioning of society by committing crimes. They fight against heroes. Plot. The villains of the criminal underworld are invited to a meeting at the Hero Association headquarters by Sitch to discuss villains working with heroes to stop Shibabawa's prophecy from coming to pass. However, the villains appeared uninterested in helping. When things turned to violence, all the gathered heroes and villains were taken down by the self-proclaimed monster Garou.

Violent Force Violent Force (暴力のフォース, "Bōryoku no Fōsu") is a ninja from the Ninja Village. He is a member of the Heavenly Ninja Party. Appearance. Violent Force was a lean man with dark hair. He wore a light-colored headband and martial arts gi. Underneath, he wore a black bodysuit which extended to his elbows and knees. His pupils possess a peculiar cross-shape. History. Violent Force was from the 42nd graduating class of the Ninja Village, known as "Heartless," alongside his fellow ninja Destructive Devastation. At some point they both joined the Heavenly Ninja Party. Plot. Neo Heroes Saga. Ninjas Arc. Violent Force appeared along with the rest of the Heavenly Ninja Party to force Speed-o'-Sound Sonic into helping find Flashy Flash and Blast. Once Violent Force and the rest of the Heavenly Ninja Party confront Sonic and Flashy Flash and the dump site, and are subsequently attacked by Sonic, they declare that Sonic is no longer on their side and attacks them. Violent Force along with the rest of the party all attack Sonic at once as they consider him to be the weaker of the ninja duo, and seem to be gaining the upper hand on him thanks to their numbers. However, once Flashy Flash starts aiding Sonic against the party members, Violent Force quickly becomes overwhelmed by Flash's skill and the duo's synergy. After Violent Force and the rest of the party are incapacitated, Flashy Flash attempts to destroy them mentally, explaining God, Blast, and "That Man," emphasizing the fact that he considered them failures as ninja. Despite this revelation, he and the rest of the party are seen laughing maniacally, as Violent Force explains that following and serving "That Man" will lead them to their ultimate resting place as ninja. Finally, he, along with the rest of the ninjas willingly give their blood and entrails to "That Man" before bursting open and being consumed by Empty Void. Abilities and Powers. As a graduate of the Ninja Village and a member of the Heavenly Ninja Party, Violent Force is a very powerful ninja. Physical Abilities. Immense Strength: As a ninja from The Village, it can be assumed that Violent Force is decently strong. Immense Speed and Reflexes: Violent Force possesses immense speed. He along with Destructive Devastation were able to catch Gale Wind and Hellfire Flame off guard and pin them in an instant. Additionally, during their fight with Flashy Flash and Sonic, he along with the other ninja were able to perform a three dimensional attack that Hellfire Flame said only elite ninja could do. Fighting Style. Ninjutsu Master: Being a graduate of The Village, Violent Force is very skilled in ninjutsu. Unlike other ninjas, he appears to focus more on his strength, as he does not fight Flashy Flash or Speed-o'-Sound Sonic with any weapons, only using his fists.

Virtual Genocide Simulation The Virtual Genocide System (VGS) is a headset designed by Dr. Kuseno. The headset is meant to catalog the data and simulates battles between the wearer and monster data stored in VGS. Overview. The VGS works by reading the brainwaves of the wearer, and simulates battles between the wearer and monster data stored in VGS. The wearer pictures the scenario and the scene of the fight in their head and VGS will carry it out in the simulation, with the resulting battle is visualized on an external monitor. Another feature of the VGS is the ability to create ghosts of the user. This is done by downloading the data of the user into the VGS and having the user fight his own ghost with the intention of strengthening the user's abilities. However, the VGS is incapable of registering certain abilities into its system, and it is also heavily affected by the user's thoughts. Examples of this are seen when Metal Bat fights Carnage Kabuto in the virtual simulation, but the battle ends when the VGS deems Metal Bat's injuries too serious to continue, failing to register Metal Bat's fighting spirit. Another example is when Zombieman's body is destroyed, leaving nothing but his head, yet the VGS continues to go on because Zombieman doesn't think his injuries are very grave. When Saitama fights himself from the day before based on the data collected, Saitama defeated him in a single punch. This could signify a few things: Regardless of what actually happened, Saitama believes the data is unreliable. Plot. Before Genos meets Gouketsu, Dr. Kuseno invents the VGS and gives it to Genos. Genos easily defeats all enemies in VGS artificially created by Dr. Kuseno. Once he defeats them, he takes his training to the next stage by uploading data collected on monsters he fought and collected data on into the VGS and engaging in simulated battles with them. Once the simulated battles are finished, Dr. Kuseno advises him to create a ghost of himself by uploading his battle data onto the VGS. Genos does as he says, and he trains diligently with his ghost. After spending some time training with his ghost, Genos wants to see his improvement and aims to test his ghost against Saitama. So he takes the VGS to Saitama's apartment and asks Saitama to test the headset. Saitama is reluctant at first, but he eventually agrees and tests out the VGS. After Saitama finishes the battle simulations, Genos is disappointed by the anticlimactic results, but realizes that it was naive to think he could understand Saitama's power through a simulation. Meanwhile, Saitama realizes he punched holes through his apartment wall during the simulation and becomes enraged. Genos wants to get more data and see the VGS work in-depth, so he contacts Hero Association and sent out a call for powerful heroes to gather at the association's headquarters to get more reference data for VGS. Sneck, Metal Bat, Zombieman, and Superalloy Darkshine all agree to test the VGS. The heroes then engage in virtual combat with Carnage Kabuto. Once all of the heroes finish battling him, Superalloy Darkshine asks Genos if there are any more powerful monsters in the VGS. Genos tells him he could upload a ghost of himself and fight the ghost, and Darkshine does just that. However, he accidentally fights Saitama's ghost and is defeated in a single punch. The VGS breaks, and the heroes believe the device is bugged. The next day, Genos comes back to Saitama's apartment with the repaired VGS and asks him to do battle with Saitama's ghost from the day before. Saitama agrees, but as he puts on the helmet, Genos begins to panic, believing if Saitama loses to his ghost, he will be affected mentally and decide to quit being a hero. Genos tries to explain to Saitama what he is getting into, but by then, the virtual battle already started. When it is over, Genos consoles him and tells Saitama it is okay to have lost to his ghost, but to the cyborg's shock, Saitama defeated the ghost in one punch. Genos marvels at this, wondering if Saitama became much more powerful than he was yesterday. Saitama tells him it was just unreliable data and goes on a short monologue describing how training in a virtual simulation will not give you any growth, with Genos vigorously taking notes.

Visitor-Murdering Panda Visitor-Murdering Panda (客全殺しパンダ, "Kyaku Zengoroshi Panda") was a Demon-level threat appeared in E-City Thrill Animal Park. It was killed by Drive Knight. Appearance. The Visitor-Murdering Panda seemingly has no visual difference from a normal . Plot. Neo Hero Saga. Neo Heroes Uprising Arc. After monsterizing in the E-City Thrill Animal Park, Visitor-Murdering Panda breaks free from its cage and spreads chaos. Its short-lived rampage is ended when Visitor-Murdering Panda encounters Drive Knight, an S-Class hero, and is killed by his arm blades in the ensuing battle. Abilities and Powers. As a Demon-level threat, it can be assumed that Visitor-Murdering Panda was a fairly powerful being. However; Drive Knight, a high-ranked S-Class hero, was able to easily defeat it.

Visualizations of Saitama Visualizations of Saitama occur when a character has been influenced by Saitama. Appearance. This influence has caused people around Saitama to envision him as an inanimate object. Personality. These thoughts of Saitama take on a Saitama-esque personality. Plot. When Tatsumaki attempted to use her psychic powers on Saitama, Fubuki mentioned how high willpower correlates to psychic resistance. She then compared Saitama's willpower as trying to pin down a boulder, envisioning Saitama as one. This happened again when Genos was talking to Drive Knight about the possible creator of the Mad Cyborg. When Genos was on the brink of going on a rampage, he remembers Saitama and sees him as a cloud, allowing Genos to calm down. Powers and Abilities. Aggravation Resistance: When angered, these visualizations can calm an individual down. Symbolic Explanation: These visualizations can be used to explain metaphors.

Void Fist Void Fist (冥躰拳, "Meitei-ken"; Viz: The Dark Body Art or Dark Corporeal Fist) is a martial art invented and taught by Master Suicho. It's primarily utilized by himself as well as his two grandchildren, Suiryu and Suiko. Overview.
